# ADR-0019: Adopt the auth.md convention as the agent-authentication surface

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-07 (work landed 2026-07-02 → 2026-07-09; backfilled 2026-07-10)
- **Deciders:** ezpds maintainers
- **Related:** [ADR-0016](0016-dynamic-lexicon-permission-set-resolution.md) · [Custos MCP plan](../../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-custos-mcp-server.md) · [scope-enforcement plan](../../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-agent-scope-enforcement.md) · [consent plan](../../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-wallet-agent-consent-and-audit.md) · `crates/pds/assets/auth.md` · MM-169/170/171/173/176/177/242/245/247/248

## Context

v0.1's auth surface was built for humans: OAuth authorization-code with DPoP,
and app passwords. Wave 8 targets autonomous agents — MCP servers and similar
clients that need a credential without a browser session. The ecosystem's
answer today is a static API key pasted into config: invisible to the user,
unscoped, and unrevocable per-agent. That contradicts the product thesis —
the user sees and controls exactly what touches their identity. The choice:
treat agents as ordinary OAuth clients, invent a bespoke onboarding API, or
adopt WorkOS's emerging **auth.md** convention for agent self-onboarding.

## Decision

We implement the auth.md convention as a first-class PDS surface:

- **Discovery.** A served `GET /auth.md` skill document, plus an `agent_auth`
  block in the RFC 8414 AS metadata advertising the identity, claim, and
  events endpoints.
- **Self-registration.** `POST /agent/identity` with three registration types,
  every one **disabled by default**: `identity_assertion` (an ID-JAG from an
  issuer on the `[agent_auth] trusted_issuers` list), `service_auth`
  (email `login_hint`), and `anonymous` (ownerless pre-claim identity).
- **Human-in-the-loop claim.** Registrations bind to an account only through a
  device-flow-style ceremony: the agent shows a `user_code`, the human
  confirms at the `verification_uri` with their own credentials, and the agent
  polls the token endpoint with the `urn:workos:agent-auth:grant-type:claim`
  grant until confirmed.
- **Token exchange.** RFC 7523 `jwt-bearer` exchanges a service-signed
  `identity_assertion` for a 5-minute sender-unconstrained Bearer token — no
  DPoP, no refresh token; agents re-exchange with a fresh assertion.
- **Scopes.** Agent tokens flow through the same granular scope grammar and
  Lexicon permission-set resolution as OAuth tokens (ADR-0016) — no parallel
  checker. Granted scopes are clamped by intersection with the operator's
  `[agent_auth] granted_scopes` profile at every mint; the default profile is
  write-to-own-repo (create/update, not delete) plus blob upload — never
  `account:*`, `identity:*`, or `rpc:*`. Agent-derived tokens carry a
  `registration_id` claim, and sensitive routes refuse them
  (`require_not_agent`).

## Consequences

- ezpds gets a spec-clean, first-party agent onboarding story; the Custos MCP
  server self-onboards against it with zero static keys in config.
- Every agent credential is user-visible, user-claimed, and user-revocable
  (the wallet's consent + audit UI over `/v1/agents`).
- The 5-minute token TTL bounds revocation latency without token-introspection
  infrastructure; the cost is one re-exchange per 5 minutes per agent.
- A default deployment exposes nothing: all three registration types are
  opt-in, and an empty issuer trust list refuses every assertion.
- We commit to an external, still-evolving convention — WorkOS's grant URN,
  event schema URIs, and document format. If auth.md moves, we track it or
  fork it deliberately.
- Claim polling state is an in-memory tracker — consistent with the
  single-process SQLite relay, but a constraint on any future multi-process
  deployment.

## Alternatives considered

- **Agents as ordinary OAuth clients with static credentials.** What the MCP
  ecosystem ships today. No self-registration, no human claim gate, no
  per-agent revocation; exactly the model the product exists to replace.
- **Full-access agent sessions.** The first cut stored
  `["com.atproto.access"]` — an exchanged agent credential "would functionally
  be a full-access session … that contradicts the product thesis and gets
  harder to fix once real agents hold tokens" (scope-enforcement plan). Scope
  clamping shipped before the onboarding tool did, as a hard prerequisite.
- **A bespoke onboarding API.** No discovery story: every agent framework
  would need a custom Custos integration. auth.md gives any agent a served
  document telling it how to onboard.
- **A parallel agent scope checker.** Rejected in favor of converging on the
  existing grammar (ADR-0016) — one enforcement path, one place to audit.

# ADR-0020: Provider-driven agent revocation via SETs, gated on the existing issuer trust list

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-09
- **Deciders:** ezpds maintainers
- **Related:** [ADR-0019](0019-authmd-agent-authentication.md) · [design plan](../../archive/design-plans/2026-07-09-agent-provider-revocation-set.md) · [test plan](../../archive/test-plans/2026-07-09-agent-provider-revocation-set.md) · MM-172 · PR #171 · `crates/pds/src/routes/agent_event.rs`

## Context

`identity_assertion` registrations are minted on a trusted issuer's word
(ADR-0019). When that provider offboards the user, decommissions the agent, or
loses a key, the PDS should stop honoring the registration promptly — not when
the operator happens to notice. RFC 8935 defines push delivery of Security
Event Tokens (RFC 8417) for exactly this. The non-obvious question isn't the
transport; it's the trust model: who may revoke, and does accepting inbound
revocations need its own opt-in?

## Decision

`POST /agent/event/notify` (the advertised `events_endpoint`) accepts RFC 8417
SETs pushed per RFC 8935. A SET is verified with the **same machinery as an
ID-JAG** — signature, `iss`, `aud` against `[agent_auth] trusted_issuers`
(`exp` only if present) — and there is **deliberately no separate opt-in
toggle**: the provider you trust to *vouch* for agents is exactly the party
you trust to *revoke* them. A SET carrying the
`…/agent/auth/identity/assertion/revoked` event type resolves the registration
by `(iss, sub)` and, in one transaction, flips it to `revoked` and writes an
audit event (`source = "provider_set"`). Delivery always answers `202`,
including for unknown or already-revoked subjects. Only `identity_assertion`
registrations are reachable — `service_auth` and `anonymous` have no
`(issuer, subject)` key and stay owner-revoked. There is no `jti` replay
store: revocation is idempotent, so a replayed SET is a no-op.

## Consequences

- A trusted provider can kill a compromised agent credential without operator
  action; the next assertion re-exchange returns `access_denied`, so live
  access ends within the 5-minute token TTL.
- Revocation authority is bundled with vouching authority. That's the point —
  but it means adding a `trusted_issuer` grants both powers at once, and
  operators should know that.
- Zero new config. A default deployment (empty trust list) refuses every SET;
  nothing is exposed until an operator deliberately trusts a provider.
- An unauthenticated caller can at most trigger one bounded signature check
  before rejection, covered by the existing global per-IP rate limiter.
- The error surface follows RFC 8935 (`{err, description}`), a third error
  envelope alongside XRPC and auth.md formats — confined to this endpoint.

## Alternatives considered

- **A separate opt-in toggle for inbound revocation.** Rejected: "Requiring a
  second opt-in would silently drop a trusted provider's revocation SETs — a
  security footgun" (design plan).
- **A `jti` dedup/replay store.** Unnecessary — the `status != 'revoked'`
  guard makes replay harmless, and a store would add state for no security
  gain.
- **RFC 8936 poll delivery, stream management, verification SETs.** Out of
  scope; one push-delivered event type is the whole contract, and it's the
  only one advertised in `events_supported`.

  action; the next assertion re-exchange returns `access_denied`, so live
  access ends within the 5-minute token TTL.
- Revocation authority is bundled with vouching authority. That's the point —
  but it means adding a `trusted_issuer` grants both powers at once, and
  operators should know that.
- Zero new config. A default deployment (empty trust list) refuses every SET;
  nothing is exposed until an operator deliberately trusts a provider.
- An unauthenticated caller can at most trigger one bounded signature check
  before rejection, covered by the existing global per-IP rate limiter.
- The error surface follows RFC 8935 (`{err, description}`), a third error
  envelope alongside XRPC and auth.md formats — confined to this endpoint.

## Alternatives considered

- **A separate opt-in toggle for inbound revocation.** Rejected: "Requiring a
  second opt-in would silently drop a trusted provider's revocation SETs — a
  security footgun" (design plan).
- **A `jti` dedup/replay store.** Unnecessary — the `status != 'revoked'`
  guard makes replay harmless, and a store would add state for no security
  gain.
- **RFC 8936 poll delivery, stream management, verification SETs.** Out of
  scope; one push-delivered event type is the whole contract, and it's the
  only one advertised in `events_supported`.

# Architecture Decision Records

An **Architecture Decision Record (ADR)** captures a single significant
architectural decision: the context that forced it, the decision itself, and the
consequences we accepted. ADRs are the *historical record* — read them to
understand why the architecture is the way it is.

## Rules

- **ADRs are immutable once `Accepted`.** Don't rewrite history. If a decision
  changes, write a *new* ADR and mark the old one `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
- **One decision per record.** If you're tempted to use "and", it's probably two
  ADRs.
- **Numbered sequentially**, zero-padded: `0001-...`, `0002-...`. The number is
  permanent; the slug describes the decision.
- **Status** is one of: `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Deferred`, `Deprecated`,
  `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`. (`Deferred` = decided in principle but intentionally
  not scheduled; it waits on a named trigger.)
- Record decisions that are *already embodied in the code* too — a decision
  doesn't have to be new to be worth recording. Backfilling the load-bearing
  ones gives future readers the "why".

## Writing a new ADR

1. Copy [`adr-template.md`](adr-template.md) to
   `NNNN-short-slug.md` (next number).
2. Fill it in. Keep it tight — an ADR is a page, not a spec. Link to
   design plans / specs for detail.
3. Add it to the log below.
4. If it changes a documented fact, update the relevant doc under
   [`../`](../) in the same change.

# v0.1 Strategy Recommendations — Index and Sequencing

Date: 2026-07-07
Status: Approved by maintainer; each linked plan is ready for implementation by an agent.

## Context

A three-track review (v0.1 gap analysis, Wave 8 / auth.md leverage, code-quality audit) found that
the v0.1 *feature* surface is essentially complete: all 25 target federation endpoints plus health,
full OAuth provider (DPoP/PAR/PKCE/JWKS/granular scopes/PRM), durable firehose with Sync v1.1, blob
GC + quotas, appview/chat proxy with read-after-write, Shamir escrow, the provisioning API, and
substantial v1.0-scope work (PDS↔PDS migration, moderation, outbound email) have all landed.

What remains is not feature work. It falls into three buckets, each with its own design plan:

## The plans

1. **[v0.1 Operational Proof](2026-07-07-v01-operational-proof.md)** — the release gate.
   Metrics (`/metrics` + federation-health gauges), a local HTTP integration harness for
   `crates/pds`, and the canonical live bsky.social migration validation run (MM-241).
   *The code is done; the proof is not.*

2. **[Agent Scope Enforcement](../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-agent-scope-enforcement.md)** — safety-critical,
   do **before** any agent exists in the wild. Today an agent credential functionally grants full
   `com.atproto.access`; per-identity `granted_scopes` are stored but not meaningfully enforced
   through the granular scope grammar.

3. **[Wallet Agent Consent and Audit](../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-wallet-agent-consent-and-audit.md)** — the
   product-thesis play. Claim-ceremony approval in Obsign, a "My agents" screen with revocation,
   and an immutable agent-action audit log.

4. **[Custos MCP Server](2026-07-07-custos-mcp-server.md)** — the differentiator. A first-party
   MCP server that self-onboards via auth.md and exposes the PDS as agent tools. Also serves as
   the end-to-end integration test for Wave 8, and gives Wave 8 a concrete finish line
   (MM-169/170/173/176 are prerequisites).

5. **[Code Quality Hardening](2026-07-07-code-quality-hardening.md)** — small, cheap-now fixes:
   async blob I/O, `Sensitive`-wrapping `admin_token`, scoped CORS for admin routes, rejection
   sampling in short-code generation, `transfer/accept` rate limiting, and a `cargo-deny` gate.

## Sequencing

```text
Code Quality Hardening ──────────────────────────────┐  (independent, do anytime, small PRs)
                                                     │
Agent Scope Enforcement ──> Wallet Consent & Audit ──┼──> Custos MCP Server
        (server closes the scope hole first)         │      (needs MM-169/170/173/176 +
                                                     │       scope enforcement to be safe)
v0.1 Operational Proof ──────────────────────────────┘  (independent; gates the v0.1 "done" call)
```

- **Agent Scope Enforcement precedes everything agent-facing.** Shipping agent onboarding (MCP,
  claim UI) while agent tokens are full-access would be practice-what-you-preach failure.
- **Operational Proof is independent** and can run in parallel with everything else. It is the
  gate for declaring v0.1 done, not a dependency of the agent work.
- **Code Quality Hardening** items are individually PR-sized and can interleave anywhere.

## Ground rules for implementing agents

These apply to every plan (they restate repo conventions from `AGENTS.md` / `crates/pds/CLAUDE.md`):

- Any new or changed PDS route **must** get a matching `.bru` file in `bruno/` (CI-enforced by
  `just bruno-check`).
- No ticket references (`MM-xxx`) in source code or CLAUDE.md files — traceability lives in
  `docs/` only.
- Routes never import routes; shared logic goes in `auth/`, `db/`, or dedicated modules.
- Tests are colocated `#[cfg(test)]` modules; router-level tests use `tower::ServiceExt::oneshot`
  against the in-memory SQLite `test_state()`.
- Run `just ci` (or `just ci-pds` where iOS crates are excluded) before pushing.
- New dependencies: justify in the PR description; `Cargo.lock` diffs are reviewed.

# MM-241 live migration round trip — runbook + record

**Status: PREPARED — not yet executed.** This document is both the checklist for the live
bsky.social migration round trip and, after execution, the permanent record of the run.
A human operator executes or supervises every leg: the run touches the real plc.directory,
the real bsky.social, and permanent `did:plc` state.

- Ticket: [MM-241](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241) (the canonical MM-207 e2e; the
  one unvalidated leg of the migration epic)
- Design: [ADR-0002](../architecture/decisions/0002-account-migration.md),
  design plan [v0.1 operational proof](../design-plans/2026-07-07-v01-operational-proof.md)
  (op-proof.AC4)
- Tooling: [`tools/interop`](../../tools/interop/README.md) (`migrate perform` / `migrate
  verify`), the Obsign wallet (inbound leg), `curl` + `jq` for the plc.directory audit checks

## The round trip

| Leg | From → To | Driver | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Inbound | bsky.social → ezpds staging | Obsign wallet UI (or goat as fallback) | PDS-signed insertion path: bsky.social's email-tokened `signPlcOperation` inserts the wallet's device key as `rotationKeys[0]` |
| (b) Outbound, self-signed | ezpds staging → ezpds production | `just interop migrate perform` | **The differentiator**: the wallet-held rotation key self-signs the PLC op; no PDS custody of the identity |
| (c) Return | ezpds production → ezpds staging | `just interop migrate perform` | Round-trip closure; nothing about the identity degraded |

Deployments: staging `https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app`, production
`https://ezpds-production.up.railway.app`.

## Required pass conditions — checked after EVERY leg

A leg is **not passed** because "the commands ran". Both checks below must be recorded per
leg (these are MM-241's acceptance criteria):

**1. plc.directory audit log shows the correct new entry for the hop.**

```sh
DID="did:plc:..."   # the migrating identity
curl -s "https://plc.directory/$DID/log/audit" | jq '.[-1] | {createdAt, nullified, operation: {rotationKeys: .operation.rotationKeys, pds: .operation.services.atproto_pds.endpoint}}'
```

Expected per leg:
- after (a): `rotationKeys[0]` is the **wallet device key** (`did:key:zDn...` held by Obsign);
  `atproto_pds.endpoint` = staging URL; entry not nullified.
- after (b): `atproto_pds.endpoint` = production URL; the op was **signed by the wallet key**
  (it must still be present in `rotationKeys`; custody unchanged).
- after (c): `atproto_pds.endpoint` = staging URL; wallet key custody still unchanged.

**2. Handle, DID document, and repo all resolve correctly against the new host.**

```sh
HANDLE="<the account handle>"
NEW_PDS="https://ezpds-production.up.railway.app"   # the leg's destination

# Handle → DID (on the new host)
curl -s "$NEW_PDS/xrpc/com.atproto.identity.resolveHandle?handle=$HANDLE" | jq .

# DID document points at the new host
curl -s "https://plc.directory/$DID" | jq '.service[] | select(.id=="#atproto_pds").serviceEndpoint'

# Repo serveable from the new host
curl -s "$NEW_PDS/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getLatestCommit?did=$DID" | jq .
```

For legs (b) and (c), `migrate verify` performs equivalent checks — run it *and* record the
audit-log check:

```sh
just interop migrate verify --name primary --target-pds "$NEW_PDS"
```

**If a leg fails:** record the failure below, file a bug (its own Linear issue, linked to
MM-241), and **stop the run**. Do not paper over a failed check to reach the next leg.

## Preconditions

- [ ] Both ezpds deployments healthy:
      `curl -s https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app/xrpc/_health` and the production
      equivalent return 200. Staging sleeps when idle — hit it once and wait for wake.
- [ ] Interop CLI installed: `just interop-setup` (Node ≥ 22.12 via the devenv shell).
- [ ] `EZPDS_ADMIN_TOKEN` for **both** deployments at hand (account creation on the
      destination mints claim codes; see per-leg notes).
- [ ] A dedicated **bsky.social test account** for the run (never the operator's real
      account), with an email inbox you control (leg (a) requires bsky.social's email token).
- [ ] Obsign wallet build on a device/simulator, signed in, holding its device key
      (leg (a)'s driver; also the custodian of the rotation key for legs (b)/(c)).
- [ ] `tools/interop/.state/state.json` backed up **before starting** (it will hold the
      did:plc rotation private key — the actual root of control; treat like a key file).
- [ ] Time budgeted: plc.directory writes are permanent; there is no dry-run mode.

## Rollback notes for the live account

There is no "undo" for a PLC op — rollback means **executing the reverse migration**, which
is exactly leg (c). If the run aborts between legs:

- After (a) only: the identity lives on staging with wallet-key custody. Acceptable
  steady-state for a test identity; optionally migrate back to bsky.social with the wallet.
- Mid-(b) failure (account created on target but DID not repointed): the source account is
  still authoritative. Deactivate the half-created destination account
  (`deactivateAccount` on the target) and retry after the bug is fixed; `migrate perform`
  is resumable in that its early steps are idempotent (reserved key, created-but-inactive
  account), but always re-run `migrate verify` against the *source* first to confirm the
  DID never moved.
- The bsky.social account: leg (a) deactivates it on bsky.social but its data remains
  exportable for 30+ days per Bluesky policy; nothing here deletes it.
- Worst case (wallet/device key lost mid-run): `state.json` (backed up above) holds the
  interop-managed rotation key for the `primary` interop identity; the migrating test
  identity's recovery follows the wallet's recovery-share flow.

## Leg (a) — inbound: bsky.social → ezpds staging

Driver: the Obsign wallet's inbound-migration flow (MM-232). There is deliberately no
interop-CLI driver for this leg. Fallback if the wallet flow is blocked: `goat account
migrate` (standard tooling) against ezpds as destination — record which driver was used.

1. In the wallet: start "Bring an identity" (inbound migration) targeting the bsky.social
   test account; destination = staging.
2. The flow will: create the deactivated destination account on staging (service-auth),
   `importRepo` + drain blobs + preferences, then request the **PDS-signed** PLC op from
   bsky.social — `requestPlcOperationSignature` emails a token to the account inbox; enter
   it in the wallet. The signed op must insert the wallet device key as `rotationKeys[0]`
   (ahead of bsky.social's recommended keys) and repoint `atproto_pds` to staging.
3. Submit; activate on staging; deactivate on bsky.social.
4. **Record both pass conditions above.** Specifically confirm `rotationKeys[0]` is the
   wallet key — this custody handoff is the entire point of the leg.

## Leg (b) — outbound self-signed: staging → production

```sh
export EZPDS_BASE_URL="https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app"   # source
export EZPDS_ADMIN_TOKEN="<staging admin token>"               # only if the account below is being created fresh

# One-time, if the migrating identity is not yet an interop-managed account on staging —
# for the MM-241 run the identity from leg (a) is adopted per the wallet flow; otherwise:
just interop create-account --name primary

just interop migrate perform --name primary --target-pds https://ezpds-production.up.railway.app
just interop migrate verify  --name primary --target-pds https://ezpds-production.up.railway.app
```

Notes:
- `migrate perform` runs the 12-step flow (reserve key on target → service-auth create →
  importRepo → blob drain → preferences → **self-signed** PLC op → submit → activate/
  deactivate). The PLC op is signed with the **locally held** rotation key — the source PDS
  never signs. That's the differentiator being proven.
- The destination (production) enforces invite codes: have the production
  `EZPDS_ADMIN_TOKEN` ready if the flow asks for a claim code.
- `migrate perform` writes a JSON report under `tools/interop/.state/reports/` — link it in
  the record below.
- **Record both pass conditions above** (audit log + resolution against production).

## Leg (c) — return: production → staging

```sh
export EZPDS_BASE_URL="https://ezpds-production.up.railway.app"   # source is now production
just interop migrate perform --name primary --target-pds https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app
just interop migrate verify  --name primary --target-pds https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app
```

Note: the interop CLI's other commands keep targeting `EZPDS_BASE_URL`, not the per-account
`pds` recorded in state — set the env var per leg as shown (see the interop README's
migration note).

**Record both pass conditions above** (audit log + resolution against staging).

## Post-run

- [ ] `just interop suite --no-interact` against staging passes with the migrated-back
      account (steady-state sanity).
- [ ] Reports linked below; `state.json` backup rotated.
- [ ] MM-241: closed with a link to this document, **or** a blocking bug filed and linked.

## Execution record

> Fill in during the run. A leg without both recorded checks is not passed.

| Leg | Date (UTC) | Operator | Driver | Audit-log check | Resolution check | Result | Artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) inbound | — | — | wallet / goat | — | — | ☐ pass ☐ fail | — |
| (b) outbound self-signed | — | — | interop CLI | — | — | ☐ pass ☐ fail | report: — |
| (c) return | — | — | interop CLI | — | — | ☐ pass ☐ fail | report: — |

DIDs used: —
Bugs filed: —
Findings / deviations: —

# Product

> Scope: this file describes the **admin-companion** mobile app (`apps/admin-companion/`),
> the operator-facing iOS admin tool for an ezpds relay. It is the design source-of-truth that
> every `/impeccable` command targeting this app reads. It is a **separate product** from the
> identity-wallet (Obsign, `apps/identity-wallet/PRODUCT.md`) and deliberately speaks a different
> design language, because its audience and its job are different.
>
> See the design plan: `docs/design-plans/2026-06-26-admin-companion-app.md`.

## Register

product

## Users

The **operator** who self-hosts an ezpds relay — and, today, administers it from a terminal with `curl`, the Bruno collection, or an SSH session into the box. They are technical: they know what a bearer token, an HTTP status code, a `did:key`, and a P-256 signature are, and they would rather read exact output than be walked through a friendly flow. This is the person who set the relay up; they are not anxious about it, they are *in command* of it.

They reach for this app in two modes, both confident and time-conscious:
1. **On-the-go admin (frequent, fast, low-drama).** Mint and hand someone an account claim code during a demo or a hallway conversation; check who's paired; glance at relay state — the things they'd normally SSH in for, done from a pocket in seconds.
2. **Loss response (rare, deliberate, not panicked).** A phone is lost or retired. The operator revokes that device from another paired device or the laptop, and confirms it can no longer act. Composed cleanup, not an alarm.

**Job to be done:** *"Let me run my relay from my pocket — do the admin action I'd normally open a terminal for, fast and unambiguously — and trust that this device can never become a liability if I lose it."*

This audience is the deliberate inverse of Obsign's. Obsign serves a possibly-non-technical person in a high-adrenaline attack; this serves a technical person in calm command. The wallet hides the machinery behind plain human stakes; this app **shows** the machinery, because the machinery is the operator's native language.

## Product Purpose

A mobile (iOS) **operator console** for an ezpds relay. It lets the person hosting the relay:
- **Generate and share account claim codes** on demand — the demo-lifesaver that motivated the app.
- **Enroll this device** as an authorized admin via QR pairing bootstrapped by the relay's master admin token.
- **Manage paired admin devices** — list them with their status, and revoke any one (the lost-phone case) without needing the phone itself.

Authentication is per-device and key-based: each phone holds a P-256 key in the Secure Enclave and **signs every request**, so there is no replayable admin secret sitting on the device. The relay's existing static master token stays as the root of trust and break-glass path.

It exists because relay administration today requires a laptop and a terminal — fine at a desk, useless in the moment you're standing in front of someone who needs a claim code. This app puts the narrow, high-value slice of operator actions where the operator actually is.

**Success looks like:** an operator pulls out their phone mid-conversation, mints a claim code, and shares it before the other person has finished asking — and never once worries that the phone in their pocket is a way into their relay. Failure is an admin tool so fiddly the operator goes back to SSH, or one whose security model makes a lost phone a breach.

## Brand Personality

A **precision operator instrument** in the lineage of a well-made developer tool — the refined-terminal lane of **Warp**, **Charm/Bubbletea**, and the dense-but-legible operator surfaces of **Linear** and **Railway**. It is the technical sibling of Obsign: same security DNA, opposite manner.

- **Three words:** Operator. Exact. Fast.
- **Voice & tone:** terse and technical. It speaks the operator's language — status codes, glyphs, monospace truth — and trusts them to read it. No onboarding warmth, no reassurance copy, no hand-holding. Confident and direct, never sloppy. Where Obsign explains, this *reports*.
- **Emotional goal:** command and speed. The operator should feel *"this is mine, it does exactly what I'd do from the terminal, and it does it faster."*
- **Where the gravitas comes from:** precision and information density done right — aligned columns, monospace where data is literal, a calm dark surface, exact spacing — **not** from chrome and **not** from hacker theatrics. The product should feel as rigorous as the keys it signs with.
- **Relationship to Obsign:** shares the OKLCH token *architecture* and the security-instrument seriousness, but forks the register — dark-first, monospace-forward, operator-terse. It is not a reskin of the wallet and must not read as one.

## Anti-references

What this must **not** look like:

- **Hacker cosplay / terminal kitsch.** No CRT scanlines, no phosphor-glow bloom, no Matrix rain, no `h4ck3r` ransom-note green-on-black, no fake boot logs as decoration. "Terminal-native" means a *refined* command surface, not a costume. The instant it looks like a movie hacker's screen, it has failed.
- **Consumer-app friendliness (Obsign's lane).** No humane onboarding carousels, no soft playful cards, no mascots, no emoji-led empty states, no reassurance copy. This audience finds that condescending.
- **Crypto / web3 hype.** Same live trap as the wallet, given the keys/DID/signature vocabulary — no neon gradients, coin iconography, or speculative-finance energy. This is infrastructure, not a token.
- **Enterprise dashboard / chart-soup.** Density is welcome, but as legible operator *output* — aligned, scannable, monospace — never as SaaS analytics widgets, gauge clusters, or KPI hero cards.
- **The low-contrast dark-theme cliché.** Dark-first is not permission for gray-on-darker-gray mush. Muddy, sub-AAA dark palettes are the most common failure of this register and are forbidden here.

## Design Principles

1. **Speak the operator's language.** Lead with the literal — status codes, glyphs, `did:key` values, exact timestamps — reported the way a terminal would, not translated into soft consumer phrasing. This audience reads output; show it the exact truth. Where Obsign hides the cryptographic machinery one tap away, this app leads with it.
2. **Density with legibility.** Operators want information per screen, not one big number. Deliver it as aligned, scannable rows — the legibility of a good `ls -l`, never chart-soup and never mush. Depth comes from precise alignment, not decoration.
3. **Speed is the feature.** The core loop — mint a claim code, share it — must complete in seconds: open, authenticate with biometrics, done. Every tap that isn't the action is friction to be removed. The win condition is "faster than opening a terminal."
4. **Practice the assurance you preach.** *(Carried verbatim from Obsign — it is the same security DNA.)* This app can mint credentials and revoke admin access. A tool that holds that power but is sloppy in its interface contradicts itself. Per-device keys, biometric-gated signing, honest revocation states, and a rigorous accessibility bar *are* the brand.
5. **Refined, not costume.** Terminal-native is an aesthetic of restraint and precision — a calm dark ground, exact monospace, disciplined color — not hacker theatrics. When in doubt, choose the version a senior infrastructure engineer would respect, not the one that looks "cyber."
6. **Honest states under loss.** The lost-phone path (a revoked device) must read unmistakably and route forward to re-pairing, never dead-end in a cryptic error. Calm competence under loss, not alarm — the operator is cleaning up, not under attack.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

- **Target WCAG 2.2 AAA, even dark-first.** 7:1 for normal text, 4.5:1 for large — held against a dark ground, where it is hardest. Dark operator palettes fail contrast constantly; this one must not. Treat AA as the floor. *(The one Obsign principle carried with zero compromise.)*
- **Status is never color alone.** Device and request state (`active` / `revoked` / `pending` / `error`) always pairs color with an explicit **glyph, text label, and position** — e.g. `● active`, `⊘ revoked`, `! error` — so a colorblind operator can never misread which device is live. A correctness requirement, not a nicety.
- **Monospace legibility under Dynamic Type.** Claim codes, `did:key`s, and device IDs scale with the system setting, stay legible at large sizes, and **never truncate silently** — they wrap (`break-all`), mirroring Obsign's Literal-Truth rule. A half-shown code is a support ticket.
- **Reduced motion honored.** Any transition has a `prefers-reduced-motion` alternative. Motion conveys state only — never decoration, and never a fake-terminal typing animation.
- **44×44pt minimum touch targets** (iOS HIG) — density is of *information*, not of tap targets. The revoke and generate actions especially get full-size, unambiguous hit areas.
- **VoiceOver.** Status, claim codes, and device IDs are announced as meaningful text, never implied by a colored dot. A code the operator is about to read aloud must be perceivable to a screen reader.

All three tasks are done. Here's where things stand.

## What I did

**Three ADRs written** (numbered in decision-date order, so the log reads chronologically):
- [ADR-0018](docs/architecture/decisions/0018-admin-signed-request-envelope.md) — Admin auth via per-device P-256 signed-request envelopes; master token stays as break-glass. Backfilled from the admin-companion design plan and `guards.rs` (landed 2026-06-28, MM-188–195).
- [ADR-0019](docs/architecture/decisions/0019-authmd-agent-authentication.md) — Adopt the WorkOS auth.md convention as the agent-auth surface (self-registration ×3 types, human claim ceremony, jwt-bearer exchange, scope clamping through the ADR-0016 grammar). The SET-revocation trust decision got its own record rather than folding in, per your call.
- [ADR-0020](docs/architecture/decisions/0020-set-revocation-trusted-issuers.md) — Provider-driven revocation via Security Event Tokens, gated on the existing `trusted_issuers` list with deliberately no second toggle.

All three are indexed in the [ADR log](docs/architecture/decisions/README.md).

**Archive sweep**: moved all nine remaining design plans, three test plans, and both implementation-plan directories to `docs/archive/` (via `git mv`, so history follows). **All three active plan directories are now empty** — a satisfying closeout signal in itself. Fixed the five cross-references that pointed at old paths (AGENTS.md, both admin-companion docs, the strategy-recs internal links, the MM-241 validation doc), plus one pre-existing broken link (the validation doc pointed at `0002-account-migration.md`, which never existed).

Nothing is committed — 38 files of staged renames + edits await your review, and the pre-existing dirty bruno files are still sitting there untouched.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The extraction pass surfaced two facts worth having in the ADRs that weren't in any plan: the admin envelope signs the *bare path only* (query strings are outside the signature — a real constraint on future admin route design), and `sweep_stale_nonces` exists but is wired to no background task. Backfilling ADRs forces exactly this kind of code-vs-plan reconciliation, which is why it's worth doing at milestone close rather than "someday."
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## ⚠️ One finding that changed priority

**The MM-241 run record was never filled in.** [docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md](docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md) still says "**Status: PREPARED — not yet executed**" and its per-leg results table is all blanks (`☐ pass ☐ fail`, no dates, no operators, no artifacts) — yet MM-241 was closed Done on 2026-07-08. The doc's own rule is "a leg without both recorded checks is not passed." Either the live run happened and the record wasn't written (fixable from memory/artifacts now, impossible in a month), or the ticket was closed before the run executed. Since this was *the* release gate for calling v0.1 done, I'd resolve it first.

## Updated closeout list

1. **Resolve the MM-241 record discrepancy** ⚠️ new, highest priority — fill in the run record if the run happened; reopen the ticket if it didn't.
2. **Commit this docs change set** (3 ADRs + log + archive sweep + link fixes) — ready to go as one commit.
3. **Merge MM-258** — the last v0.1 issue, in review.
4. **Decide the dirty bruno files** — `list_repos.bru` (modified) and `environments/production.bru` (untracked; check for a real admin token before committing).
5. **Stale doc touch-ups** — AGENTS.md still lists the admin-companion `/impeccable` scan + simulator demo as open; `pds.dev.toml:76` still calls the anonymous agent flow "not yet implemented" (it shipped in MM-242). Small; could ride along with any commit.
6. **Wire `sweep_stale_nonces` to a background task** — genuine loose end the ADR work surfaced; tiny ticket, storage-only impact.
7. **Linear hygiene** — wave labels/milestones for MM-278–285; file the license-decision ticket.
8. **Release cut** after MM-258: `just set-version` → `just release` → `just deploy-production`.
9. **Reconcile the milestone map's v0.2 section** with the actual next-phase direction (did:web cluster vs. desktop enrollment) before planning the next milestone.

Which one next? If it's #1, tell me what actually happened with the live run and I'll update the record accordingly.

{"id":"MM-241","title":"Validate live bsky.social migration round trip (canonical MM-207 e2e)","description":"## Overview

The canonical end-to-end validation described in the <issue id="4cfdf611-180c-43ee-b3eb-b10a5407e87f" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-207/account-migration-pdspds-full-inbound-outbound-support-epic">MM-207</issue> epic — the only piece of that epic not covered by code + tests. All implementation legs are merged (server XRPC surface, wallet self-signed identity leg, path detection, orchestration, UI, ezpds-as-source e2e test, outbound email); this ticket tracks proving them against the **live network**.

## The round trip (per ADR-0002)

With [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>) accepting inbound migrations:

1. **(a) Inbound:** import a [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>) identity into ezpds via the PDS-signed insertion path (email-tokened `signPlcOperation` on [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>); the op inserts the wallet's device key as `rotationKeys[0]`).
2. **(b) Outbound, self-signed:** migrate that identity *out* of ezpds to a second PDS (staging → production, or vice versa), with the wallet self-signing the PLC op — **this middle leg is the proof of the differentiator**.
3. **(c) Return:** migrate back.

## Tooling notes

* `tools/interop` has `migrate perform` / `migrate verify` for the outbound (self-signed) leg against a live deployment.
* There is currently **no inbound-migration driver** in the interop CLI — the inbound leg is driven from the wallet UI (<issue id="0e291b18-5162-4c8d-9e39-e3b22a031708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-232/wallet-outbound-migration-ui-obsign">MM-232</issue>) or standard tooling (goat / official client) against ezpds as destination.
* Both ezpds deployments (staging + production) are available as the two PDS endpoints for the middle leg.

## Acceptance

* Each leg's DID audit-log entry on [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) shows the expected rotation-key custody at every step.
* Handle/DID/repo resolve to the correct PDS after each leg (`migrate verify` or equivalent).
* Findings (including any interop bugs against [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>)) recorded here; bugs get their own issues.

# claim_token_ttl_secs = 600        # lifetime of a claim token

# auth_time_max_age_secs = 3600     # ID-JAG auth_time older than this → login_required
# jwks_cache_ttl_secs = 3600        # how long a fetched issuer JWKS (jwks_url) is reused

input.title: Wire sweep_stale_nonces to a background task
input.description:
## Context

Surfaced while backfilling [ADR-0018](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/blob/main/docs/architecture/decisions/0018-admin-signed-request-envelope.md) (admin signed-request envelopes): every device-signed admin request inserts a row into `admin_nonces` for anti-replay. `sweep_stale_nonces` exists in `crates/pds/src/db/admin_devices.rs` (implemented, unit-tested, with a supporting `idx_admin_nonces_seen_at` index) but is **not wired to any background task** — it's called only from tests. The table grows unbounded with admin traffic.

Not a security issue: anti-replay doesn't depend on the sweep — the `(device_id, nonce)` primary key enforces single use. This is storage reclamation only, which is why it's low priority.

## Spec

- Schedule `sweep_stale_nonces` as a periodic background task in the server startup path, following the existing pattern (`account_reaper`, `firehose_gc`).
- Retention only needs to exceed the ±60s timestamp window (`ADMIN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` in `crates/pds/src/auth/guards.rs`) — a nonce older than the window can never verify again, so anything beyond a few minutes is safe. A generous margin (e.g. sweep hourly, delete rows older than 1 hour) keeps it trivially correct.
- Log sweep outcomes at debug/trace like the other sweepers.

## Acceptance

- A long-running relay's `admin_nonces` row count stays bounded under continuous admin traffic.
- Replay rejection behavior is unchanged (existing guard tests still pass).

Based on the search results, I can provide you with a clear answer to your question:

**No, archived issues do not count toward Linear's 250 issue limit on the free plan.**

Linear's free plan includes 250 non-archived issues, and archived issues do not count toward the 250 active-issue cap. More specifically, archived issues are unlimited and auto-archive timing is configurable in team settings.

This means that teams that aggressively archive completed issues and run lean backlogs can use Linear's free tier indefinitely. Everything's done and pushed. Here's the state of play and my recommendation on the Linear plan.

## Sync + push ✅

Local `main` rebased cleanly onto the MM-258 merge and pushed — `173675d2` (docs closeout ×3 commits) plus `b00060fb` (gitignore, below) are on GitHub and the tangled mirror. CI will run and, on green, staging deploys.

## Local ticket archive ✅

`linear-export/mm-issues.json` — **all 282 MM issues ever created**, full descriptions, 103 comments, labels, states, milestones, relations, timestamps (plus `summary.json` with the stats). Two things to know:

- **It's deliberately untracked and now gitignored** (`b00060fb`): this repo is public (the iOS CI depends on that), so committing ticket contents would publish them. If you want it under version control, a private repo or local backup is the right home.
- Because it captures every label assignment, the wave↔issue mapping is now durable outside Linear regardless of what you do to the labels.

## The numbers, and my recommendation

You're at **224 of 250 active issues — 90% of the free-plan cap**. But archived issues don't count toward the limit ([Linear pricing](https://linear.app/pricing), [Quackback breakdown](https://quackback.io/blog/linear-pricing)), and **206 of your 224 active issues are Done/Canceled/Duplicate**. Archiving them drops you to **~18 active** — the cap stops mattering for a year or more, with zero deletion.

**Archiving:** I can't execute this — the MCP surface has no archive mutation and Bash writes to Linear are blocked in this environment — but it's about 30 seconds in the UI: filter team MM by status Done → select all → Archive. Also worth flipping on **Settings → team MM → auto-archive closed issues** (e.g. 1 month) so this never accumulates again. The two Duplicates (MM-268, MM-273) archive along with them.

**Wave labels: my recommendation is keep them.** Labels don't consume issue quota, so removing them frees nothing — the motive would be purely decluttering the label picker. Once the Done issues are archived, the wave labels live almost entirely on archived issues where they cost nothing and remain the searchable wave↔history mapping. Deleting a label strips it from archived issues too and is irreversible in Linear. If you do want the picker decluttered, Waves 0–6 + Wave 3 are 100% complete and safe to delete now that the export preserves the mapping — but I'd leave Wave 7 (MM-241, MM-286 open) and Wave 8 alone either way. One consequence to note: the `linear_wave_status` tally tool won't see archived issues, so wave history in Linear effectively freezes — which is fine, since the waves are done and the export has the record.

**Stray hygiene the export surfaced:** MM-178/179/180 (tangled-extension work) have **no project at all**, and MM-153 belongs to project `atbb` — decide whether those live somewhere or archive with the rest. And MM-278–284 still need wave labels/milestones (the earlier hygiene item) — say the word and I'll tag those via the MCP now.

## Remaining closeout list

1. **Run MM-241** — the live migration round trip + fill in the record table *(yours; the last v0.1 gate)*
2. **Linear UI pass** *(yours, ~2 min)* — bulk-archive Done issues, optionally enable auto-archive; label deletion per your call above
3. **Tag MM-278–285** with waves/milestones — *I can do this now*
4. **File the license-decision ticket** (pre-v1.0) — *I can do this now*
5. **Release cut** once MM-241 passes: `just set-version` → `just release` → `just deploy-production`
6. **Reconcile the milestone map's v0.2 section** with the actual next-phase direction before planning the next milestone

{"id":"MM-278","title":"did:web account hosting — minimum path to migrate did:web:malpercio.dev onto Custos","description":"## Goal

Move the operator's primary account, `did:web:malpercio.dev`, onto Custos. Because the operator controls [malpercio.dev](<http://malpercio.dev>)'s web hosting independently of the PDS, **Custos does not need to serve** `.well-known/did.json` **for this** — the DID document stays wherever [malpercio.dev](<http://malpercio.dev>) is hosted and is edited there. (Custos-served did.json + the `did:web:obsign.org` apex scenario are deferred — see the sibling "later" issue.)

## Already works (verified 2026-07-10)

* **did:web resolution**: `identity_resolution.rs:82-100` dispatches on method; `resolve_web_did_document` (442-477) is a complete SSRF-guarded resolver.
* **Migration-in is method-agnostic**: `createAccount` migration mode (`create_account_xrpc.rs:396-515`) resolves the DID document and verifies the `#atproto` key without inspecting the method. `importRepo`, `listMissingBlobs`, `checkAccountStatus`, `activateAccount`, `getRecommendedDidCredentials` all exist and are method-agnostic.
* **Storage**: `did` is an opaque TEXT primary key everywhere (`db/CLAUDE.md`).

## Migration choreography (simpler than did:plc — no email token, no PLC op)

1. `createAccount(did: did:web:malpercio.dev)` with old-PDS service-auth JWT → deactivated account + session
2. `importRepo` (CAR from `sync.getRepo` on the old PDS) + blob drain via `listMissingBlobs`/`uploadBlob`
3. `getRecommendedDidCredentials` → operator edits `https://malpercio.dev/.well-known/did.json` by hand: `#atproto_pds` service endpoint → Custos, `#atproto` verificationMethod → the reserved signing key
4. `refreshIdentity` / cache refresh so Custos sees the updated doc
5. `checkAccountStatus` → `activateAccount`

## Minimum work items

- [ ] **Guard the PLC-only endpoints** for non-`did:plc` accounts: `signPlcOperation`, `submitPlcOperation`, `requestPlcOperationSignature` currently fail confusingly (404 on the [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) audit-log fetch). Return an explicit "not a did:plc" error.
- [ ] **Cached-doc refresh path**: after the operator edits the externally-hosted did.json, ensure the `did_documents` cache row is refreshed (does `refreshIdentity` cover it end-to-end for a did:web?) and the `#identity` firehose frame is emitted.
- [ ] **End-to-end test**: integration test of the full migration choreography with a did:web DID (mock the did.json host), mirroring the ADR-0002 canonical migration test.
- [ ] **Handle**: keep `@malpercio.dev` — verification stays on the operator's own domain (DNS TXT `_atproto.malpercio.dev` or its own `/.well-known/atproto-did`); zero PDS work. Confirm the handles-table binding path accepts a handle the PDS host doesn't serve.
- [ ] **Wallet honesty (Obsign)**: gate the did:plc-only surfaces (PLC monitoring, recovery, claim, Shamir) for a did:web identity instead of silently showing nothing. Per the ADR-0003 critique: did:web has no rotation hierarchy, no audit log, no recovery window — say so in-app.
- [ ] **ADR-0003 amendment**: the ADR says "did:web is not offered as an account identity method" — amend/supersede to "not *minted*, but *hosted* for user-owned domains" (consistent with the superseded provisioning spec's exit-liability rule, `docs/provisioning-api-spec.md:44-47`: never host a did.json for a domain the user doesn't control).

## References

* ADR-0002 (wallet-authorized migration), ADR-0003 (did:plc as DID method)
* `docs/provisioning-api-spec.md:44-47` — bring-your-own-domain did:web prior art
* Interop harness already uses `did:web:malpercio.dev` as the operator identity (`tools/interop/README.md`)","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-278/didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate-didwebmalperciodev-onto","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-278-didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate","createdAt":"2026-07-10T20:47:09.886Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-10T22:43:34.723Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["did:web"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

{"id":"MM-279","title":"Managed did:web hosting — optionally serve did.json for user-owned domains, with attested safeguards","description":"## Goal (updated 2026-07-10)

The operator currently runs a web server whose sole purpose is hosting `https://malpercio.dev/.well-known/did.json`. Offer **opt-in managed hosting**: Custos serves the DID document on behalf of the user, letting them retire that server — while keeping the identity trust model honest. Only ever for **user-owned domains** (the provisioning spec's exit-liability rule): exit is always a DNS repoint away.

## Integration levels

1. **Path-level** — user keeps their site; routes only `/.well-known/did.json` (optionally `/.well-known/atproto-did`) to Custos via CDN/proxy rules.
2. **Domain-level** — whole domain points at Custos: did.json + handle verification + content-negotiated identity page all served Host-keyed; standalone web server retired.

## Core work

- [ ] `GET /.well-known/did.json` route, keyed on request Host → opted-in account whose DID is `did:web:{host}` → render from `did_documents` (pattern: `atproto_did.rs` is already Host-keyed). New `routes/did_json.rs` + `app.rs` + `.bru`.
- [ ] Opt-in flag + domain verification before serving (e.g. confirm the doc Custos would serve matches what the domain currently resolves to externally).
- [ ] Authenticated did-doc **update path that isn't a PLC op** (direct edit of the stored document, `#identity` firehose frame) — today all doc mutations flow through `submitPlcOperation`.
- [ ] TLS/deployment: add the custom domain to the Railway service (manual is fine for v1; multi-tenant self-serve would need Cloudflare-for-SaaS / Caddy on-demand TLS later).

## The trust model (the safeguards ARE the feature)

Moving hosting from an independent server to Custos removes independence; these restore it, honestly:

1. **Wallet co-signing as policy** `rotationKeys[0]` — Custos refuses to serve an updated did.json unless the diff is device-key-signed (reuse Obsign's 4-point signed-operation review). Optional wallet-signed **freeze** (pin the doc N days).
2. **Shadow audit log** — hash-linked, dual-signed (PDS + device key) history of every served version. Option: store history as records in the user's own repo → replicates via firehose, rides along in CAR exports automatically.
3. **External monitoring** — Obsign polls the *served* doc from outside (plc_monitor.rs analog) + CT-log watch, DNSSEC/registrar-lock checks, domain-expiry countdown. Detects a tampered doc even though Custos is the host, because the wallet knows what the device key last approved.
4. **DNS repoint as instant override** — managed did:web hosting recreates the two-tier custody model: Custos serving = `rotationKeys[1]`, user's domain control = `rotationKeys[0]`, override instant (no 72h window needed). The **exit kit** (one-tap archive: did.json + signed history + repo CAR + blob manifest) makes the repoint target a restore, not a scramble.
5. **Content-negotiated apex** — resolvers get did.json; browsers get a sealed-credential identity page in the marketing register.

**Honest caveat (brand: report the literal truth):** none of this changes did:web's root of trust — domain registration controls the identity; signed history proves tampering, it does not prevent it.

## Sequencing constraint

Migrate first (<issue id="8547c9de-cf87-4a2f-964a-53d71d9dabb8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-278/didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate-didwebmalperciodev-onto">MM-278</issue>) with the doc on the existing server; then enable managed hosting → Custos serves a byte-identical doc → flip routing → verify external resolution → retire the server. Never move hosting mid-migration; the doc must stay continuously resolvable.

## Deferred note kept here: the @obsign.org apex collision

ATProto supports hostname-form did:web only, so `did:web:obsign.org` = one account per hostname — and the PDS's default *server* DID is `did:web:{public_host}` (`crates/common/src/config.rs:96`). If an account ever takes the apex identity where the PDS is hosted: host the PDS at a subdomain (e.g. `pds.obsign.org`) and/or set `server_did` explicitly (<issue id="70f422d7-4740-4f6f-b6a6-429540684b26" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-202/set-ezpds-server-did-in-production-to-enable-jwt-audience-validation">MM-202</issue>), reverse-proxying the apex well-knowns to the PDS — the same serving machinery this issue builds.

## References

* ADR-0003 (did:plc as DID method — amendment tracked in <issue id="8547c9de-cf87-4a2f-964a-53d71d9dabb8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-278/didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate-didwebmalperciodev-onto">MM-278</issue>)
* `docs/provisioning-api-spec.md:44-47` — exit-liability rule
* <issue id="70f422d7-4740-4f6f-b6a6-429540684b26" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-202/set-ezpds-server-did-in-production-to-enable-jwt-audience-validation">MM-202</issue> — explicit `server_did` in production
* `docs/2026-06-30-pds-phase-0.1-gap-and-competitive-analysis.md:94` — did-method-specific recovery messaging","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-279/managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user-owned-domains","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-279-managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user","createdAt":"2026-07-10T20:47:37.037Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-10T22:43:38.564Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["did:web"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

{"id":"MM-285","title":"Wallet did:web ceremony — the 2×2: new/existing DID × self/Custos-hosted, with device-key escrow","description":"## Goal (captured 2026-07-10)

Extend Obsign's onboarding to walk a user through **did:web** identities across two levers — **new vs. existing did.json** × **self-hosted vs. Custos-hosted** — reusing the existing device-key + Shamir-escrow ceremony. Sibling issues: <issue id="8547c9de-cf87-4a2f-964a-53d71d9dabb8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-278/didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate-didwebmalperciodev-onto">MM-278</issue> (migrate did:web:malpercio.dev in), <issue id="dffcbf51-33df-4fc6-88aa-41a1c6868bd1" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-279/managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user-owned-domains">MM-279</issue> (managed did.json hosting + safeguards).

## Shared spine (all four cells)

* Wallet generates/reuses the **device key** (Secure Enclave / software fallback) — the existing ceremony machinery.
* **Shamir 2-of-3 escrow unchanged and method-agnostic**: Share 1 → iCloud Keychain, Share 2 → Custos escrow (single share reveals nothing), Share 3 → user offline.
* **Publish the device key in the did.json as an additional verificationMethod.** This is the keystone: it makes <issue id="dffcbf51-33df-4fc6-88aa-41a1c6868bd1" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-279/managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user-owned-domains">MM-279</issue>'s shadow audit log third-party-verifiable and gives "you hold the top key" public meaning despite did:web having no rotationKeys.
* `#atproto` verification method = Custos's reserved signing key (`reserveSigningKey`); `#atproto_pds` = Custos endpoint.

## The four cells

1. **New × Custos-hosted** — wallet composes the full did.json → guided DNS step (domain or well-known path → Custos) → Custos verifies external resolution, starts serving (<issue id="dffcbf51-33df-4fc6-88aa-41a1c6868bd1" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-279/managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user-owned-domains">MM-279</issue>) → account created.
2. **New × self-hosted** — wallet composes and **exports** the did.json (share-sheet plugin) with upload instructions, then **polls until the served doc resolves and matches byte-for-byte** before account creation.
3. **Existing × Custos-hosted** — <issue id="8547c9de-cf87-4a2f-964a-53d71d9dabb8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-278/didweb-account-hosting-minimum-path-to-migrate-didwebmalperciodev-onto">MM-278</issue> migration + <issue id="dffcbf51-33df-4fc6-88aa-41a1c6868bd1" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-279/managed-didweb-hosting-optionally-serve-didjson-for-user-owned-domains">MM-279</issue> hosting takeover; device-key adoption rides in the takeover's first doc update.
4. **Existing × self-hosted** — the did:web analog of `claim.rs` (which inserts the device key as `rotationKeys[0]` into a foreign did:plc): wallet generates key + escrows shares, presents a **4-point-review-style diff** of the did.json changes (add device-key VM, repoint `#atproto`/`#atproto_pds`), exports the updated JSON, poll-verifies the live doc.

## Custos-side prerequisite: a new did:web mint path

Migration mode can't serve cell 1/2 — it authenticates via a service-auth JWT from the *old* PDS, and a brand-new DID has none. {"id":"MM-280","title":"Labeler watching: flag hosted accounts + notify the operator","description":"Inspired by [brookie.blog](<http://brookie.blog>)'s [PDS Operator](<https://tangled.org/brookie.blog/pds-operator>) — its headline feature is "watches labelers and DMs you when an account gets flagged," with flagged accounts floating to the top of the account list.

We have nothing like this. The loop:

**Server (relay/PDS side)**

* Configurable list of watched labeler DIDs (any labeler, not just Bluesky's — PDS Operator makes this pluggable).
* Subscribe to each labeler's label stream (or poll `com.atproto.label.queryLabels`), match label events against hosted DIDs, persist flagged state per account.
* Expose flagged state on the operator accounts listing (`GET /v1/admin/accounts`) so clients can sort flagged accounts first.

**admin-companion (Brass Console)**

* Accounts screen: flagged accounts sort to the top with an explicit flag indicator (label value + labeler + time — never color alone, per DESIGN.md).
* Notification when a hosted account gets flagged. PDS Operator DMs the operator on Bluesky; for us the natural channel is APNs push to paired admin devices — but that's a larger lift (push infra), so an in-app flagged-accounts badge is a reasonable first slice, with push as a follow-on.

This is the most valuable single feature of the set — it turns the accounts list from a neutral roster into a spam/abuse triage view.","projectMilestone":{"id":"8c2537ab-8f05-4ad7-9e24-76d5ae9f7bde","name":"v1.0 — Production Launch"},"priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-280/labeler-watching-flag-hosted-accounts-notify-the-operator","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-280-labeler-watching-flag-hosted-accounts-notify-the-operator","createdAt":"2026-07-10T20:50:18.657Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-10T22:43:45.116Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Mobile: Admin Companion","Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

{"id":"MM-281","title":"Relay status readout: is the relay actually crawling/indexing us?","description":"Inspired by [brookie.blog](<http://brookie.blog>)'s [PDS Operator](<https://tangled.org/brookie.blog/pds-operator>), which has a relay-status feature — notably because her own PDS silently fell behind the relay the day before she shipped it and she found out the hard way.

Today we have `/metrics` but no federation-health visibility: nothing tells the operator whether the relay has seen the PDS recently, whether it's indexing new commits, or how far behind the relay's cursor is.

**Server**

* A relay-health check the operator surface can expose: e.g. compare our sequencer head against what the relay reports for our hostname (`com.atproto.sync.getHost` / listHosts on the relay), plus last-crawl/last-seen info. Expose via a `/v1/admin/relay-status` style endpoint (admin-authed, Bruno entry per repo convention).

**admin-companion (Brass Console)**

* A relay status block — likely on Home for the active server: reachable / crawling / behind-by-N / not seen since T. Status expressed with text + icon, never color alone.
* "Request crawl" action is a natural companion if we expose it.

{"id":"MM-282","title":"Operator-initiated password reset for hosted accounts","description":"Inspired by [brookie.blog](<http://brookie.blog>)'s [PDS Operator](<https://tangled.org/brookie.blog/pds-operator>), which includes password resets in its operator toolkit.

We have the destructive half of account recovery — `POST /v1/admin/accounts/:id/revoke-credentials` sweeps sessions, app passwords, OAuth grants, and transfer-device tokens — but no constructive half: after the kill switch fires, the operator has no way to get the legitimate holder back in. The self-serve `requestPasswordReset` flow depends on the account having working email, which is exactly what may be unavailable/compromised in the scenarios where the operator steps in.

**Server**

* Admin-authed endpoint (master token or signed device request, like the other `/v1/admin/*` routes) to either set a temporary password directly or mint a one-time reset token the operator hands to the user out-of-band. One-time token is the safer design (operator never knows the resulting password).
* Bruno entry + route pattern comments per `crates/pds/CLAUDE.md`.

**admin-companion (Brass Console)**

* Action on the account detail screen alongside the existing revoke-credentials kill switch, biometric-gated like claim-code reveal, with the token surfaced via `CodeOutput` for out-of-band sharing.

Together with revoke-credentials this completes the compromised-account runbook: lock everything out, then re-admit the real holder.","projectMilestone":{"id":"8c2537ab-8f05-4ad7-9e24-76d5ae9f7bde","name":"v1.0 — Production Launch"},"priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-282/operator-initiated-password-reset-for-hosted-accounts","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-282-operator-initiated-password-reset-for-hosted-accounts","createdAt":"2026-07-10T20:50:40.332Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-10T22:43:49.691Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Mobile: Admin Companion","Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

{"id":"MM-284","title":"Decide + surface human signup invite management in Brass Console","description":"Inspired by [brookie.blog](<http://brookie.blog>)'s [PDS Operator](<https://tangled.org/brookie.blog/pds-operator>), which manages signup invites from the operator dashboard.

Brass Console currently surfaces **claim codes** (agent onboarding) but not human-signup invites. Server-side we have partial invite plumbing — `com.atproto.server.createInviteCode`/`createInviteCodes`/`getAccountInviteCodes` routes and `V004__claim_codes_invite.sql` — but the console has no view of it, and it's not settled whether standard signup on our deployments is (or should be) invite-gated.

This is decision-shaped first, feature-shaped second:

1. **Decide:** is human signup on staging/production open, invite-gated, or closed? (Same-day context from the PDS Operator thread: operators report hand-created spam accounts that captchas don't stop — invite gating is the lever that actually works there, and it's what makes labeler-flag monitoring (<issue id="42c3071c-50ab-478a-a72c-7c13fe01a686" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-280/labeler-watching-flag-hosted-accounts-notify-the-operator">MM-280</issue>) a manageable queue instead of a firehose.)
2. **If invite-gated:** a Brass Console invites screen — mint/list/disable invite codes per server, share via the existing share-sheet plugin, reusing the claim-codes screen patterns (`CodeOutput`, biometric gate).
3. **If not:** document the decision and close.

Scope note: claim codes and invite codes should stay visibly distinct in the UI — one admits agents, the other admits humans.","projectMilestone":{"id":"8c2537ab-8f05-4ad7-9e24-76d5ae9f7bde","name":"v1.0 — Production Launch"},"priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-284/decide-surface-human-signup-invite-management-in-brass-console","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-284-decide-surface-human-signup-invite-management-in-brass","createdAt":"2026-07-10T20:51:09.770Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-10T22:43:54.234Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Mobile: Admin Companion","Feature"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

input.title: Decide the project license
input.description:
## Context

The only v0.1-plan item that never got a ticket. `docs/v01-issue-plan.md` closes with:

> **License:** TBD — decision deferred to pre-v1.0. Options under consideration: AGPL-3.0, Apache-2.0/MIT dual, or BSL-style.

The repo is **public on GitHub with no LICENSE file**, which legally means all-rights-reserved despite being world-readable — worth resolving before v1.0's "BYO PDS binary" milestone item, since self-hosting distribution is meaningless without a license that permits it.

## Decision inputs

- **AGPL-3.0** — network copyleft; hosted forks must publish source. Common for self-hostable server products defending against closed SaaS rehosting.
- **Apache-2.0/MIT dual** — maximum adoption, patent grant via Apache-2.0; no protection against closed rehosting.
- **BSL-style** — source-available with a delayed open conversion; protects a future managed offering but is not OSI-open and complicates community contribution.
- The workspace `Cargo.toml` currently has `publish = false` and no `license` field; whatever is chosen sets `[workspace.package] license` and adds the LICENSE file.
- Note: `deny.toml`'s license allowlist governs *dependencies* and is unaffected, but a copyleft choice for the project itself should be sanity-checked against the vendored/forked code in the tree (e.g. the swift-rs patch copy, vendored Tauri plugins) whose upstream licenses must permit relicensing-adjacent distribution.

## Deliverables

- LICENSE file at repo root (+ per-crate if dual-licensing)
- `[workspace.package] license` field
- README/marketing-site licensing note if the choice affects the self-hosting story

2	name: reference-linear-access
3	description: "How to read and write Linear (team MM / ezpds) from Claude Code — MCP for writes, API key for reads"
4	metadata:

10	Linear team is **MM** ("Mal's Machinations"), project **ezpds**. Two access paths from Claude Code:
11	
12	- **Writes** (status changes, comments, create/update issues): use the `plugin:linear:linear` MCP. It needs OAuth — on a fresh session only `mcp__plugin_linear_linear__authenticate` is loaded; call it, have the user authorize in the browser, then the real tools appear. `save_issue(id:"MM-98", state:"Done")` and `save_comment(issueId:"MM-98", body:...)` take identifiers directly; `state` accepts a name/type/ID.
13	- **Reads**: `LINEAR_API_KEY` is in `.env.local` (gitignored). `set -a; source .env.local; set +a` then POST GraphQL to `https://api.linear.app/graphql` with header `Authorization: $LINEAR_API_KEY`. Good for wave/label scans.
14	
15	**Gotchas:**
16	- The `linear_wave_status` / `linear_list_issues` / `linear_update_issue` tools named in AGENTS.md are **Pi** extension tools (`.pi/extensions/linear/index.ts`), NOT available to Claude Code. Don't try to call them — replicate their GraphQL instead, or use the MCP.
17	- **Writes via Bash** (curl/python hitting the Linear API) are **hard-blocked** by the auto-mode classifier as external-system writes, even with user authorization. Writes must go through the authenticated MCP.
18	- zsh mangles `!` inside heredoc'd GraphQL (`String!` → `String\!`); inline values or put the query in a file written via the Write tool.
19	- The exhaustive `issues(first: 250)` wave-status scan can return HTTP 500; page smaller or filter by label (e.g. `labels: { name: { eq: "Wave 4: Repo + Blobs" } }`).
20	- **Wave labels are team-scoped to MM, not workspace-level.** `list_issue_labels` with NO `team` arg returns an incomplete set (only a few labels) — call it with `team:"MM"` to see the full wave list. Their real names carry a suffix: `Wave 0: Scaffolding`, `Wave 1: Running Server`, `Wave 2: Auth`, `Wave 3: Identity` AND `Wave 3: Key Sovereignty` (two Wave-3 labels), `Wave 4: Repo + Blobs`, `Wave 5: Federation`, `Wave 6: App Proxy`, `Wave 7: Hardening`, `Wave 8: auth.md`. `save_issue(labels:[...])` matches on the **exact full name** — `labels:["Wave 7"]` silently no-ops (returns `labels:[]`); use `"Wave 7: Hardening"`.
21	
22	Related: [[project_relay_cicd]].

name: reference-linear-access
description: "How to read and write Linear (team MM / ezpds) from Claude Code — MCP for writes, API key for reads"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: bdaadf6b-adac-4639-958e-edc6feda2454
---

Linear team is **MM** ("Mal's Machinations"), project **ezpds**. Two access paths from Claude Code:

- **Writes** (status changes, comments, create/update issues): use the `plugin:linear:linear` MCP. It needs OAuth — on a fresh session only `mcp__plugin_linear_linear__authenticate` is loaded; call it, have the user authorize in the browser, then the real tools appear. `save_issue(id:"MM-98", state:"Done")` and `save_comment(issueId:"MM-98", body:...)` take identifiers directly; `state` accepts a name/type/ID.
- **Reads**: `LINEAR_API_KEY` is in `.env.local` (gitignored). `set -a; source .env.local; set +a` then POST GraphQL to `https://api.linear.app/graphql` with header `Authorization: $LINEAR_API_KEY`. Good for wave/label scans.

**Gotchas:**
- The `linear_wave_status` / `linear_list_issues` / `linear_update_issue` tools named in AGENTS.md are **Pi** extension tools (`.pi/extensions/linear/index.ts`), NOT available to Claude Code. Don't try to call them — replicate their GraphQL instead, or use the MCP.
- **Writes via Bash** (curl/python hitting the Linear API) are **hard-blocked** by the auto-mode classifier as external-system writes, even with user authorization. Writes must go through the authenticated MCP.
- zsh mangles `!` inside heredoc'd GraphQL (`String!` → `String\!`); inline values or put the query in a file written via the Write tool.
- The exhaustive `issues(first: 250)` wave-status scan can return HTTP 500; page smaller or filter by label (e.g. `labels: { name: { eq: "Wave 4: Repo + Blobs" } }`).
- **Wave labels are team-scoped to MM, not workspace-level.** `list_issue_labels` with NO `team` arg returns an incomplete set (only a few labels) — call it with `team:"MM"` to see the full wave list. Their real names carry a suffix: `Wave 0: Scaffolding`, `Wave 1: Running Server`, `Wave 2: Auth`, `Wave 3: Identity` AND `Wave 3: Key Sovereignty` (two Wave-3 labels), `Wave 4: Repo + Blobs`, `Wave 5: Federation`, `Wave 6: App Proxy`, `Wave 7: Hardening`, `Wave 8: auth.md`. `save_issue(labels:[...])` matches on the **exact full name** — `labels:["Wave 7"]` silently no-ops (returns `labels:[]`); use `"Wave 7: Hardening"`.

**Free-plan capacity (learned 2026-07-10):** the 250-issue cap counts only NON-archived issues — archiving frees quota, deletion is never needed (user deleted atbb issues needlessly before learning this). The Linear UI offers no manual archive and auto-archive waits ≥1 month after close, but the GraphQL `issueArchive` mutation archives immediately. A full local export (all 282 MM issues + comments) and a user-runnable archive script live in `linear-export/` in the repo (gitignored — repo is public, never commit it): `node linear-export/archive-done.mjs [--yes]`. Claude cannot run the archive script (Bash Linear writes blocked) — the user runs it.

Both items done, plus the deletion workaround. Summary:

## Linear tagging ✅

- **did:web cluster** — created a new `did:web` team label (sealing-wax gold, naturally) and applied it to MM-278, MM-279, and MM-285 (which kept its wallet label). I deliberately left their **milestone empty**: assigning them to a phase is exactly the v0.2-reconciliation decision still on the list, and I didn't want to pre-empt it.
- **Operator console five** — MM-280–284 got `Mobile: Admin Companion` + `Feature` labels and the **v1.0 — Production Launch** milestone, since they're production-operations scope (moderation, federation health, account recovery, audit, invites).

## License ticket ✅

[MM-287 — Decide the project license](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-287/decide-the-project-license), v1.0 milestone, Medium. One thing I put in the ticket worth seeing now: the repo is **public with no LICENSE file**, which legally means all-rights-reserved despite being world-readable — and v1.0's "BYO PDS binary" item doesn't work without a license permitting self-hosting, so the two are coupled.

## About the archive problem — you may not need deletions

The UI won't let you archive manually and auto-archive waits a month, but the **GraphQL API's `issueArchive` mutation archives immediately** — UI limitations usually don't apply to it. I can't run Linear writes from here, but I left you a script (in the gitignored `linear-export/`, so it stays private):

```
node linear-export/archive-done.mjs        # dry run — lists the ~206 closed issues it would archive
node linear-export/archive-done.mjs --yes  # archives them (reversible, unlike delete)
```

It reads `LINEAR_API_KEY` from `.env.local`, targets only closed (Done/Canceled/Duplicate) unarchived MM issues, and paces itself under the rate limit. If the mutation turns out to be plan-gated it'll fail loudly on the first issue and you've lost nothing — deletion remains the fallback. Sorry about the atbb issues; deleted issues aren't recoverable via the API, though everything in team MM as of today is preserved in the export.

## Remaining closeout list

1. **Run MM-241** — live migration round trip + fill in the record table *(yours; the last v0.1 gate)*
2. **Try `archive-done.mjs --yes`** — should take you from 224 → ~18 active issues without deleting anything *(yours, one command)*
3. **Release cut** once MM-241 passes: `just set-version` → `just release` → `just deploy-production`
4. **Reconcile the milestone map's v0.2 section** with the actual direction (the did:web cluster now being labeled makes that conversation easier) — then milestone the did:web issues accordingly

Items 3 and 4 I can help with when you get there — #4 in particular would make a good short design session.

input.title: License housekeeping: declare AGPL-3.0 in Cargo metadata
input.description:
## Context (corrected)

This ticket was originally filed claiming the repo had no LICENSE file, based on the stale `docs/v01-issue-plan.md` note ("License: TBD — decision deferred to pre-v1.0"). That was wrong: **`LICENSE` exists at the repo root and is AGPL-3.0** (added in commit `0169a85c`). The decision is made; what remains is declaring it in the places tooling and readers look.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Add `license = "AGPL-3.0-only"` (or `"AGPL-3.0-or-later"` — pick deliberately; the LICENSE file alone doesn't distinguish) to `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml` so every crate inherits it via `{ workspace = true }`.
- [ ] Sanity-check the vendored/forked code in the tree (swift-rs patch copy, vendored Tauri plugins) — their upstream permissive licenses are compatible with AGPL distribution, but their own license files/headers should stay intact.
- [ ] Mention the license in the README / marketing site self-hosting story if/when BYO PDS ships (v1.0 milestone item).
