## Troubleshooting

### `cargo tauri ios dev` fails with "Connection refused"

You launched the Xcode build manually (clicking Run in Xcode) instead of through `cargo tauri ios dev`. Xcode's "Build Rust Code" phase calls `cargo tauri ios xcode-script`, which connects back to the `cargo tauri ios dev` process via JSON-RPC. There is no server to connect to if the build was not initiated by `cargo tauri ios dev`.

**Fix:** Always use `cargo tauri ios dev` from the terminal. Do not click Run in Xcode.

---

### `error: can't find crate for 'core'` — `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` target not installed

The Nix `rust-default` package (used by `languages.rust` in devenv) does not ship iOS cross-compilation stdlibs. This was the historical state of the project before the rustup migration.

**Fix:** Already resolved. `devenv.nix` uses `pkgs.rustup` with project-local `RUSTUP_HOME`/`CARGO_HOME`. On first `nix develop`, `enterShell` runs `rustup toolchain install` which reads `rust-toolchain.toml` and installs `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` stdlib automatically.

If you see this after a fresh clone: make sure you entered the dev shell from the **workspace root** (not from `apps/identity-wallet/`) so that `CARGO_HOME` resolves correctly.

---

### `error: tool 'simctl' not found` or `xcrun simctl list` fails

The Nix devenv's Darwin setup hooks override `DEVELOPER_DIR` (and `SDKROOT`) to a Nix apple-sdk stub that has no runtime tools. The `xcbuild` xcrun shim in PATH delegates to `$DEVELOPER_DIR/usr/bin/xcrun` — if `DEVELOPER_DIR` points at a Nix stub, it fails.

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. `devenv.nix`'s `enterShell` sources `apps/identity-wallet/scripts/ios-env.sh`. The catch: `/usr/bin/xcode-select -p` and `/usr/bin/xcrun` both **honor `DEVELOPER_DIR` above the system Xcode selection**, so calling them by absolute path is not enough — they echo the Nix stub straight back. `ios-env.sh` first **unsets `DEVELOPER_DIR` when it points into `/nix/store`**, so `xcode-select -p` falls through to the real Xcode selection; it then re-exports `DEVELOPER_DIR` to that real path. (A genuine Xcode-provided `DEVELOPER_DIR` — not under `/nix/store` — is left untouched, so the Xcode Run Script keeps Xcode's own value.)

If you still see this: verify with `echo $DEVELOPER_DIR` inside the dev shell. If it shows a Nix store path, exit and re-enter the shell from the workspace root.

---

### `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` (Tauri ios-api build)

Swift Package Manager sandboxes its manifest compilation using `sandbox-exec`. On macOS 26 (Tahoe), `sandbox_apply()` returns `EPERM` in this context, causing `swift-rs`'s build script (used by Tauri) to fail with "Failed to compile swift package Tauri".

**Fix:** Already resolved and applied automatically. A local patch of `swift-rs` 1.0.7 at `apps/identity-wallet/swift-rs-patch/` adds `--disable-sandbox` to the `swift build` invocation inside `SwiftLinker::link`. The workspace `Cargo.toml` wires this in via `[patch.crates-io]`. See `docs/ios-upstream-bugs.md` for details. Remove the patch entry when swift-rs ships a fix upstream.

---

### `Failed to update the excludes stack to see if a path is excluded` (Xcode user script sandbox)

Xcode 14+ enables `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING=YES` by default in generated projects, wrapping Run Script build phases in `sandbox-exec`. On macOS 26 (Tahoe), this sandbox blocks Cargo's `readdir()` calls during package fingerprinting, producing:

```
error: failed to determine package fingerprint for build script for identity-wallet v0.1.0
Caused by: Failed to update the excludes stack to see if a path is excluded
```

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template sets `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: NO`, which every `cargo tauri ios init` renders into the generated project; `just ios-check` verifies the setting is in place.

---

### `Undefined symbols ... _SC*` / `_ASWebAuthenticationSession*` — an Apple framework not linked at `Ld`

The Rust code compiles, then Xcode's link step fails with `Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:` naming Apple framework symbols — e.g. `_SCDynamicStore...` / `_SCNetworkReachability...` (Apple's `SystemConfiguration.framework`, which the `system-configuration` crate needs — pulled in transitively by `hickory-resolver` for system DNS config and `reqwest` for system proxy detection), or `_ASWebAuthenticationSessionErrorDomain` (Apple's `AuthenticationServices.framework`, which the vendored `tauri-plugin-auth-session` needs via `objc2-authentication-services` / `ASWebAuthenticationSession`).

Host builds (`cargo test` / `cargo build`) link fine because **rustc** does the final link and honors the crate's `#[link(name = "...", kind = "framework")]`. On iOS the crate is built as a `staticlib` (`libapp.a`) and **Xcode** does the final link — it never sees that embedded directive, so the framework must be declared in the Xcode project or the symbols stay undefined. A `build.rs` `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework=...` does NOT help (same staticlib → Xcode gap).

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template renders `OTHER_LDFLAGS = "$(inherited) -framework SystemConfiguration -framework AuthenticationServices"` from `bundle > iOS > frameworks` in `tauri.conf.json` (the same list also produces xcodegen `sdk:` link dependencies), and `just ios-check` verifies every listed framework. The historical footgun this design removes: `bundle.iOS.frameworks` used to seed only a FRESH project.yml, because `cargo tauri ios init` preserves an existing one — with the custom template, project.yml is re-rendered from config on every init, so the config is now the enforced mechanism. To link another Apple framework a new Rust dep requires, **add it to `bundle > iOS > frameworks` in `tauri.conf.json`** and re-run `cargo tauri ios init` + `just ios-postinit` — never hand-edit `OTHER_LDFLAGS` in the generated project (a second `OTHER_LDFLAGS` assignment for the same build config shadows, not appends to, the first, silently dropping a framework — `just ios-check` detects that state).

---

### `libapp.a ... is not permitted` / `Invalid bundle structure` on TestFlight upload

`cargo tauri ios build` succeeds and `xcrun altool` then rejects the upload (HTTP 409): *"The 'Obsign.app/libapp.a' binary file is not permitted. Your app cannot contain standalone executables or libraries."* (tauri#13578.)

cargo-mobile2 lists the `Externals` directory (which holds the Rust staticlib `libapp.a`) as a project source with **no explicit `buildPhase`**, so XcodeGen infers `resources` and copies the raw `.a` into the `.app` — which App Store validation forbids. The library is also (correctly) **linked** via the separate `framework: libapp.a` entry + `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS`, so excluding it from resources is safe.

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template sets `Externals → buildPhase: none`, so xcodegen never emits a `libapp.a in Resources` entry (the `framework: libapp.a` link dependency is kept). `just ios-check` verifies both layers.

---

### `base64: invalid option -- 'o'` during `cargo tauri ios build` signing

The build reads `IOS_CERTIFICATE` and fails decoding it: `base64: invalid option -- 'o'`. In the Nix dev shell, GNU coreutils `base64` shadows macOS's BSD `base64` in `PATH`, but Tauri's cert decode uses BSD-only flags (`-i`/`-o`). (CI is unaffected — the runner has no Nix.)

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. `scripts/ios-env.sh` (under `EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1`) shims `/usr/bin/base64` ahead of the Nix one via a tiny symlink dir on `PATH` — surgical (only `base64`), leaving every other Nix tool untouched.

input.title: Post-migration/recovery DID-doc cache stores the W3C document — home badge degrades to "Unknown" (no rotationKeys)
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (r) — the migration itself succeeded and verified clean on plc.directory (endpoint → obsign.org, device key at rotationKeys[0]), but the wallet's home card then showed the **"Unknown"** custody badge for the migrated identity.

## Root cause

The wallet caches a **PLC-format** DID document per identity (`{did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, verificationMethods, services}` — what `claim::submit_claim` builds and the create flow synthesizes). `IdentityListHome.isDeviceKeyRoot` reads `didDoc.rotationKeys[0]`; `extractPdsFromPlcDoc` reads the `services` map.

But the post-submit cache refresh in **`migrate::submit_migration_op`** and **`recovery::submit_recovery_override`** fetches `GET {plc.directory}/{did}` — the **W3C DID document** (`@context/id/alsoKnownAs/verificationMethod/service[]`), which carries **no `rotationKeys`** and a different service shape — and stores it via `store_did_doc`, clobbering the good PLC-format cache. Result: `deviceKeyIsRoot === null` → "Unknown" badge (and the card's PDS-host line degrades too).

## Fix

Fetch `GET {plc.directory}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document — exactly the cached shape: `did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, services, verificationMethods`) in both `submit_migration_op` and `submit_recovery_override`. Wallet-only change; simulator-testable; no server deploy.

Note: an identity whose cache was already clobbered (the leg (r) throwaway) stays "Unknown" until the next flow re-stores its doc — acceptable, it's disposable.

[MM-300](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home) — found by the MM-241 leg (r) rehearsal. The migration itself succeeded and verified clean on plc.directory, but the wallet's home card then showed the **\"Unknown\"** custody badge for the migrated identity.

The wallet's per-identity DID-doc cache uses the **PLC data shape** (\`{did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, verificationMethods, services}\`) — it's what the create and claim flows store, and what the readers parse: \`IdentityListHome.isDeviceKeyRoot\` reads \`rotationKeys[0]\`, \`extractPdsFromPlcDoc\` reads the \`services\` map. But the post-submit refresh in \`migrate::submit_migration_op\` and \`recovery::submit_recovery_override\` fetched \`GET {plc}/{did}\` — the **W3C document** (\`@context/id/verificationMethod/service[]\`, no \`rotationKeys\`) — and stored that, clobbering the good cache. Custody badge → null → \"Unknown\".

## Fix

Both refreshes fetch \`GET {plc}/{did}/data\` — the PLC data document, exactly the cached shape. Two-line URL change plus comments.

## Tests

The three end-to-end tests (migrate ×1, recovery ×2, httpmock) now mock \`/{did}/data\` with PLC-data-shaped bodies; the migrate test additionally asserts the cached doc carries \`rotationKeys\` (the regression pin). Full \`identity-wallet\` suite: 343 pass (+3 ignored socket-binding tests run manually, all pass). Clippy \`-D warnings\` + fmt clean.

Wallet-only — no server deploy. Note: an identity whose cache was already clobbered (the leg (r) throwaway) stays \"Unknown\" until a future flow re-stores its doc; it's disposable." 2>&1 | tail -1

52	/// Identifies the fork point — the last legitimate operation before unauthorized changes began.
53	///
54	/// Walks backward through the audit log from the target unauthorized operation CID.
55	/// For multiple sequential unauthorized ops, returns the earliest fork point
56	/// (the last device-key-signed op before the first unauthorized op in the sequence).
57	///
58	/// Returns `(fork_point_entry, pre_unauthorized_state)` where:
59	/// - `fork_point_entry` is the last legitimate AuditEntry (its CID becomes the `prev` for the counter-op)
60	/// - `pre_unauthorized_state` is the VerifiedPlcOp representing the state to restore
61	pub(crate) fn find_fork_point(
62	    audit_log: &[AuditEntry],
63	    unauthorized_op_cid: &str,
64	    device_key: &DidKeyUri,
65	) -> Result<(AuditEntry, crypto::VerifiedPlcOp), RecoveryError> {
66	    // Find the index of the unauthorized operation in the audit log.
67	    let target_idx = audit_log
68	        .iter()
69	        .position(|e| e.cid == unauthorized_op_cid)
70	        .ok_or(RecoveryError::UnauthorizedChangeNotFound)?;
71	
72	    if target_idx == 0 {
73	        return Err(RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
74	            message: "Cannot recover from the genesis operation".to_string(),
75	        });
76	    }
77	
78	    // Walk backward from the operation BEFORE the unauthorized one to find the
79	    // last operation signed by the device key. If multiple unauthorized ops are
80	    // in sequence, we skip past all of them to find the earliest fork point.
81	    for i in (0..target_idx).rev() {
82	        let entry = &audit_log[i];
83	        let op_json =
84	            serde_json::to_string(&entry.operation).map_err(|e| RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
85	                message: format!("Failed to serialize operation: {e}"),
86	            })?;
87	
88	        // Try to verify with the device key. If verification succeeds,
89	        // this is the last legitimate operation (the fork point).
90	        match crypto::verify_plc_operation(&op_json, std::slice::from_ref(device_key)) {
91	            Ok(verified) => return Ok((entry.clone(), verified)),
92	            Err(_) => continue, // Not signed by device key, keep looking
93	        }
94	    }
95	
96	    Err(RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
97	        message: "No device-key-signed operation found before the unauthorized change".to_string(),
98	    })
99	}

MM-288 (merged 2026-07-11, PR #185 → main 6b3cb8a0) made the wallet's OAuth identity fixed:
- `client_id` = `https://identitywallet.obsign.org/oauth/client-metadata.json` (const `CANONICAL_CLIENT_ID` in `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/pds_client.rs`), no longer derived from the configured Custos. Loopback dev is the one exception (derives `{base}/oauth/client-metadata.json`).
- redirect scheme = `org.obsign.identitywallet:` — the client_id host in **reverse-FQDN order**, which the atproto OAuth spec requires for native private-use redirects and third-party AS's (bsky.social) enforce. iOS bundle id stayed `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` (provisioning untouched); both URL schemes coexist in `Info.ios.plist` during the transition.
- Custos serves the canonical doc (`routes/oauth_client_metadata.rs`) + seeds it (migration **V042**, V013 kept for old builds), and its PAR now enforces the same reverse-FQDN rule for discoverable https client_ids.
- Reserved handle names are operator-configurable: `Config::reserved_handles` / `EZPDS_RESERVED_HANDLES` / NixOS `reservedHandles`, default `identitywallet,about`. Enforced in registration, updateHandle's served-domain branch, AND migration mode (`handle::reserved_on_served_domain`, gated on served-domain).

**Production deploy DONE 2026-07-11: v0.4.3 (`dc57eedd`) is live on obsign.org** carrying MM-288 + MM-289 (+ MM-286 nonce sweep, MM-287 AGPL metadata). Verified live: `https://identitywallet.obsign.org/oauth/client-metadata.json` serves the self-referencing canonical doc (the `*.obsign.org` wildcard routes it to Custos), and a bsky.social PAR replay with the canonical client_id + `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback` returns a `request_uri` (was `invalid_redirect_uri` pre-fix). **MM-241 leg (a)'s only remaining dependency is the wallet build**: a TestFlight build from `4fecfded` or later (has the password source-login + new URL scheme; old builds fail — their scheme can't complete the callback). Related: [[project_ios_oauth_deeplink]], [[project_federation_readiness]].

**MM-241 leg (a) PASSED 2026-07-11 23:46 UTC** — on-device run of the TestFlight build from `c7373fc3` (carries MM-291 no-body procedures, MM-293 claim DID registration, MM-294 secp256k1 verification). plc.directory newest op: wallet key `did:key:REDACTED` at `rotationKeys[0]` of `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7`, bsky `zQ3…` keys preserved, services untouched; handle/repo/profile resolution intact. **Deviation recorded in the runbook (`docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md`, committed `63c60e28`): the shipped flow is claim-only** — no staging account, no `atproto_pds` repoint, no bsky deactivation (runbook steps 1–3 predate the phased custody-first design). Legs (b)/(c) as scripted assume an interop-managed identity already on staging; the real identity is still on bsky with its rotation key in the wallet — (b)/(c) need re-scoping before execution.

**MM-289 (second leg-(a) blocker, past MM-288) — MERGED 2026-07-11 (PR #190, squash `4fecfded` on main; Linear Done).** The wall: PLC/identity ops (`requestPlcOperationSignature`/`signPlcOperation`) need a FULL session; bsky.social's OAuth ceiling for a third-party client is `transition:generic`, which grants no identity ops — so no OAuth token bsky.social issues can drive the claim flow. Fix (ADR-0021): the wallet **claim** flow's source login is now a one-shot password `com.atproto.server.createSession` → full-session Bearer client (`claim::authenticate_source_pds` → `pds_client::create_session` → `OAuthClient::new_bearer`), replacing the OAuth PKCE login (`prepare_pds_auth`/`complete_pds_auth` deleted). Custos was **tightened to spec**: `oauth_scopes::allows_identity` no longer accepts `transition:generic` (only granular `identity:*` or a full `com.atproto.access` session passes `require_identity`) — `allows_email`/`allows_account`/etc. unchanged, so the outbound-migration orchestrator's OAuth source token (repo/blob/status only, self-signed identity leg) is unaffected. App passwords are correctly refused (lesser scope). Error surfacing fixed: an insufficient-scope refusal now shows as `ClaimError::InsufficientScope`, not the misleading "failed to send verification email". OAuth stays the auth for the create flow + outbound migration source login. Create flow + home unaffected.

**Everything's recorded and shipped. Where things stand:**

**Leg (r): PASS**, written into the [runbook](docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md) (commit `81fd337d`) with both conditions verified — the self-signed op repointed the DID to production with the device key held at `rotationKeys[0]`, the repo serves from production at the same rev staging froze at, and the handle resolves. The wallet's entire outbound orchestrator is now live-proven end to end.

**The "Unknown" badge: diagnosed and fixed** — [MM-300](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home), [PR #202](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/202). The migration and recovery flows were refreshing the wallet's per-identity cache from plc.directory's *W3C* document, which has no `rotationKeys` — clobbering the PLC-format doc every reader expects. Both now fetch `/{did}/data`; tests pin the endpoint and the cached shape. Wallet-only, so no deploy — it rides the next TestFlight build. (The throwaway's cache stays "Unknown" since it was clobbered pre-fix; it's disposable. The staging-domain handle you noticed is correct behavior — migration preserves the name.)

**What's left of MM-241** — the real identity, on your phone:
- **Leg (b)**: bsky → staging. Wants the next TestFlight build (with MM-300 so post-migration state displays right) — merging #202 triggers that automatically.
- **Legs (c)/(d)**: staging → production → staging. All server-side deploy dependencies already met (both environments on the v0.4.4 train + staging has MM-299).

Final scoreboard for leg (r): five bugs found and fixed (DPoP scheme, consent-form scope loss, preferences lifecycle gate, non-resumable createAccount, DID-doc cache shape) plus one adjacent security finding (MM-296, repo-write binding gap, still open in the backlog). The rehearsal leg cost a few staging round-trips and caught every one of them before your phone or the real identity was ever at risk — exactly what it was designed for. Merge #202 when you're ready and the TestFlight watcher routine kicks in for leg (b).

input.title: Claim flow caches empty rotationKeys (W3C doc parse) — migrate button hidden for claimed identities; add cache self-heal
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (b) prep: on the phone, the claimed bsky.social identity shows no "Migrate to another PDS" button (and the "Unknown" custody badge).

## Root cause

Same disease as MM-300, third vector. `+page.svelte` wires `onmigrate` only when `deviceKeyIsRoot === true`, which `IdentityListHome` derives from the cached doc's `rotationKeys[0]`. `claim::submit_claim`'s post-claim re-fetch goes through `discover_pds`, which parses plc.directory's **W3C** document into `PlcDidDocument` — whose `rotation_keys` is `#[serde(default)]` and documented as "Empty if only populated from the W3C DID Document". The claim flow then persists a PLC-shaped doc with `rotationKeys: []` → badge "Unknown" → migrate entry hidden, even though plc.directory shows the device key at `rotationKeys[0]`.

## Fix (extends PR #202)

1. `claim::submit_claim` re-fetches `GET {plc}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document) and caches that, like the MM-300 fix did for migrate/recovery. Shared `PdsClient::fetch_plc_data_document` helper used by all three.
2. **Self-heal**: existing installs already have poisoned caches (the phone's claimed identity, the sim throwaway). New `refresh_did_doc` IPC command (fetch `/data` + re-store); `IdentityListHome.loadData` invokes it best-effort whenever the cached doc is missing or has no `rotationKeys`, so stale caches repair on the next home load with no user action.

Wallet-only; ships in the same build as MM-300.

52	/// Identifies the fork point — the last legitimate operation before unauthorized changes began.
53	///
54	/// Walks backward through the audit log from the target unauthorized operation CID.
55	/// For multiple sequential unauthorized ops, returns the earliest fork point
56	/// (the last device-key-signed op before the first unauthorized op in the sequence).
57	///
58	/// Returns `(fork_point_entry, pre_unauthorized_state)` where:
59	/// - `fork_point_entry` is the last legitimate AuditEntry (its CID becomes the `prev` for the counter-op)
60	/// - `pre_unauthorized_state` is the VerifiedPlcOp representing the state to restore
61	pub(crate) fn find_fork_point(
62	    audit_log: &[AuditEntry],
63	    unauthorized_op_cid: &str,
64	    device_key: &DidKeyUri,
65	) -> Result<(AuditEntry, crypto::VerifiedPlcOp), RecoveryError> {
66	    // Find the index of the unauthorized operation in the audit log.
67	    let target_idx = audit_log
68	        .iter()
69	        .position(|e| e.cid == unauthorized_op_cid)
70	        .ok_or(RecoveryError::UnauthorizedChangeNotFound)?;
71	
72	    if target_idx == 0 {
73	        return Err(RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
74	            message: "Cannot recover from the genesis operation".to_string(),
75	        });
76	    }
77	
78	    // Walk backward from the operation BEFORE the unauthorized one to find the
79	    // last operation signed by the device key. If multiple unauthorized ops are
80	    // in sequence, we skip past all of them to find the earliest fork point.
81	    for i in (0..target_idx).rev() {
82	        let entry = &audit_log[i];
83	        let op_json =
84	            serde_json::to_string(&entry.operation).map_err(|e| RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
85	                message: format!("Failed to serialize operation: {e}"),
86	            })?;
87	
88	        // Try to verify with the device key. If verification succeeds,
89	        // this is the last legitimate operation (the fork point).
90	        match crypto::verify_plc_operation(&op_json, std::slice::from_ref(device_key)) {
91	            Ok(verified) => return Ok((entry.clone(), verified)),
92	            Err(_) => continue, // Not signed by device key, keep looking
93	        }
94	    }
95	
96	    Err(RecoveryError::SigningFailed {
97	        message: "No device-key-signed operation found before the unauthorized change".to_string(),
98	    })
99	}

gh pr edit 202 --title "fix(wallet): PLC data-document cache everywhere + self-heal (MM-300, MM-301)" --body "## Problem

Two vectors of one disease, both found by MM-241 testing: the wallet's per-identity DID-doc cache expects the **PLC data shape** (\`{did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, verificationMethods, services}\`) — its readers are the home card's custody badge (\`rotationKeys[0]\`) and \`extractPdsFromPlcDoc\` — but three flows were refreshing it with the **W3C document**, which carries no \`rotationKeys\`:

- **[MM-300](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home)**: \`migrate::submit_migration_op\` and \`recovery::submit_recovery_override\` fetched \`GET {plc}/{did}\` directly → migrated identity showed the \"Unknown\" badge (leg (r) sim).
- **[MM-301](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-301/claim-flow-caches-empty-rotationkeys-w3c-doc-parse-migrate-button)**: \`claim::submit_claim\` re-fetched via \`discover_pds\`, whose \`PlcDidDocument.rotation_keys\` is empty by construction from the W3C parse → the claimed bsky identity on the phone cached \`rotationKeys: []\`, so the **\"Migrate to another PDS\" entry** (gated on \`rotationKeys[0] == device key\`) never appeared — blocking MM-241 leg (b).

## Fix

- New \`PdsClient::fetch_plc_data_document\` (\`GET /{did}/data\`) is the single canonical cache-refresh fetch; **claim, migrate, and recovery** all use it (no more hand-rolled W3C fetches).
- **Cache self-heal** for already-poisoned installs (the phone's claimed identity, the sim throwaway): new \`refresh_did_doc\` IPC command; \`IdentityListHome.loadData\` invokes it best-effort whenever a cached doc is missing or has empty \`rotationKeys\`. Stale caches repair on the next home load — no re-claiming, no user action.

## Tests

- Claim/migrate/recovery submit tests mock \`/{did}/data\` with PLC-data-shaped bodies and assert the cached doc carries \`rotationKeys\` (regression pins).
- The orchestrator's ignored full-pipeline test mock updated to \`/data\` (the first commit had broken it; masked by a filter that doesn't match \"migration\" — caught and fixed here).

\`cargo test -p identity-wallet\`: 343 pass + all mock-based ignored tests pass (the 2 remaining ignored failures require a live localhost Custos, pre-existing). Clippy \`-D warnings\`, fmt, \`pnpm check\` (0 errors), \`pnpm test\` (64) all clean.

Wallet-only — no server deploy. On-device effect after this build: the bsky identity's badge flips to \"Root key\" and the migrate button appears on first home load." 2>&1 | tail -1

{"id":"MM-301","title":"Claim flow caches empty rotationKeys (W3C doc parse) — migrate button hidden for claimed identities; add cache self-heal","description":"## Found by

<issue id="10c8aa2a-f2fe-433f-9ba4-fed81b554e7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e">MM-241</issue> leg (b) prep: on the phone, the claimed [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>) identity shows no "Migrate to another PDS" button (and the "Unknown" custody badge).

## Root cause

Same disease as <issue id="d87c4698-7a8e-4373-92bb-64dffb8ec5d8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home">MM-300</issue>, third vector. `+page.svelte` wires `onmigrate` only when `deviceKeyIsRoot === true`, which `IdentityListHome` derives from the cached doc's `rotationKeys[0]`. `claim::submit_claim`'s post-claim re-fetch goes through `discover_pds`, which parses [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>)'s **W3C** document into `PlcDidDocument` — whose `rotation_keys` is `#[serde(default)]` and documented as "Empty if only populated from the W3C DID Document". The claim flow then persists a PLC-shaped doc with `rotationKeys: []` → badge "Unknown" → migrate entry hidden, even though [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) shows the device key at `rotationKeys[0]`.

## Fix (extends PR #202)

1. `claim::submit_claim` re-fetches `GET {plc}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document) and caches that, like the <issue id="d87c4698-7a8e-4373-92bb-64dffb8ec5d8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home">MM-300</issue> fix did for migrate/recovery. Shared `PdsClient::fetch_plc_data_document` helper used by all three.
2. **Self-heal**: existing installs already have poisoned caches (the phone's claimed identity, the sim throwaway). New `refresh_did_doc` IPC command (fetch `/data` + re-store); `IdentityListHome.loadData` invokes it best-effort whenever the cached doc is missing or has no `rotationKeys`, so stale caches repair on the next home load with no user action.

Wallet-only; ships in the same build as <issue id="d87c4698-7a8e-4373-92bb-64dffb8ec5d8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home">MM-300</issue>.","priority":{"value":1,"name":"Urgent"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-301/claim-flow-caches-empty-rotationkeys-w3c-doc-parse-migrate-button","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-301-claim-flow-caches-empty-rotationkeys-w3c-doc-parse-migrate","createdAt":"2026-07-12T14:47:02.992Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-12T15:01:13.006Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-07-12T15:01:12.863Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"In Review","statusType":"started","labels":[],"attachments":[{"id":"6597e983-df59-4381-be70-c8e48fe06a22","title":"fix(wallet): PLC data-document cache everywhere + self-heal (MM-300, MM-301)","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/202"}],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","assignee":"Malpercio","assigneeId":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

**Done — [PR #202](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/202) now carries both MM-300 and MM-301, all gates green.**

What shipped in the second commit:

{"id":"MM-300","title":"Post-migration/recovery DID-doc cache stores the W3C document — home badge degrades to "Unknown" (no rotationKeys)","description":"## Found by

<issue id="10c8aa2a-f2fe-433f-9ba4-fed81b554e7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e">MM-241</issue> leg (r) — the migration itself succeeded and verified clean on [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) (endpoint → [obsign.org](<http://obsign.org>), device key at rotationKeys[0]), but the wallet's home card then showed the **"Unknown"** custody badge for the migrated identity.

The wallet caches a **PLC-format** DID document per identity (`{did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, verificationMethods, services}` — what `claim::submit_claim` builds and the create flow synthesizes). `IdentityListHome.isDeviceKeyRoot` reads `didDoc.rotationKeys[0]`; `extractPdsFromPlcDoc` reads the `services` map.

But the post-submit cache refresh in `migrate::submit_migration_op` and `recovery::submit_recovery_override` fetches `GET {plc.directory}/{did}` — the **W3C DID document** (`@context/id/alsoKnownAs/verificationMethod/service[]`), which carries **no** `rotationKeys` and a different service shape — and stores it via `store_did_doc`, clobbering the good PLC-format cache. Result: `deviceKeyIsRoot === null` → "Unknown" badge (and the card's PDS-host line degrades too).

Fetch `GET {plc.directory}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document — exactly the cached shape: `did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, services, verificationMethods`) in both `submit_migration_op` and `submit_recovery_override`. Wallet-only change; simulator-testable; no server deploy.

Same disease as <issue id="d87c4698-7a8e-4373-92bb-64dffb8ec5d8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-300/post-migrationrecovery-did-doc-cache-stores-the-w3c-document-home">MM-300</issue>, third vector. `+page.svelte` wires `onmigrate` only when `deviceKeyIsRoot === true`, which `IdentityListHome` derives from the cached doc's `rotationKeys[0]`. `claim::submit_claim`'s post-claim re-fetch goes through `discover_pds`, which parses [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>)'s **W3C** document into `PlcDidDocument` — whose `rotation_keys` is `#[serde(default)]` and documented as "Empty if only populated from the W3C DID Document". The claim flow then persists a PLC-shaped doc with `rotationKeys: []` → badge "Unknown" → migrate entry hidden, even though [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) shows the device key at `rotationKeys[0]`.

Shared `PdsClient::fetch_plc_data_document` helper used by all three.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/pr-review-comments

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

content.text:
Yes — that's exactly right, and it's the deliberate design difference between the two flows:

- **The claim flow (leg a)** used a username/password login screen inside the app, because its next steps were PLC identity operations (`requestPlcOperationSignature`/`signPlcOperation`) that bsky.social only permits with a full session — no OAuth token a third-party app can obtain grants those (that was the whole MM-289 saga, ADR-0021).
- **The outbound migration flow (leg b)** doesn't need any identity operation from bsky — the PLC op is **self-signed by your phone's Secure Enclave key**, which is the entire point of what you're about to prove. All it needs from bsky as source is repo export, blob fetch, preferences, service auth, and the final deactivate — all covered by a standard OAuth grant (`transition:generic`). So the source login is the in-app OAuth sheet (ASWebAuthenticationSession), not a password form.

As for why you jumped straight to the *authorize* page without typing credentials: the OAuth sheet shares Safari's cookie jar, so if you've signed into bsky.social in Safari before (including during earlier testing), bsky recognizes the session and skips its login form, going directly to consent. If you'd never logged in there, you'd see bsky's own username/password page first, then this same consent screen.

Two quick checks before you tap Authorize:

1. **The account named on the consent page is `malpercio-obsign.bsky.social`** — if Safari's cookie is for a different bsky account, the flow would authorize the wrong one (the orchestrator does re-check the DID matches the migration, so a mismatch fails safely, but better to catch it at the screen).
2. The requesting app should identify as the wallet (the canonical `identitywallet.obsign.org` client).

Then authorize and let it run: destination `https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app` + your staging claim code. The pipeline from there is the one leg (r) already proved — the only new seam is bsky-as-source honoring `transition:generic` on `getServiceAuth`, preferences export, and `deactivateAccount`. If it trips, the unified-log line will name the seam, same drill as always.

content.text:
Full picture, cleanly reproduced and probes revoked:

| Credential tier | `getServiceAuth` for `createAccount` |
|---|---|
| Full session (password `createSession`) | ✅ mints |
| **Privileged** app password | ✅ mints |
| Plain app password / **OAuth `transition:generic`** ← your phone | ❌ `insufficient access` |

So bsky gates minting a `createAccount` service token at the **privileged** tier, and the wallet's outbound source login sits below it. This is MM-289's sibling: the orchestrator's design assumed `transition:generic` covers everything a *self-signed* migration needs from the source — true for repo/blobs/preferences/deactivate, false for this one mint. Leg (r) couldn't catch it because Custos's `require_rpc` is laxer than the reference and lets `transition:generic` mint any method (an MM-292-family divergence that masked the wall).

Filing the ticket with this evidence. On the fix, two real options:

1. **Password source login for outbound migration** (my recommendation): swap `prepare_source_auth`/`complete_source_auth` OAuth for the claim flow's password `createSession` machinery (`authenticate_source_pds` already exists, with 2FA handling and the HTTPS/account-match guards). Consistent with ADR-0021's logic — migrating away is exactly the class of account-authority operation the reference gates behind a real session. Honest UX: "sign in with your password to move your account." Works identically against bsky and Custos sources, so legs (b)/(c)/(d) all use one path.
2. **Request `transition:chat.bsky` in the OAuth scope** to reach the privileged tier — technically works, but semantically absurd (asking for DM access to migrate) and fragile against future reference changes. I'd reject it.

Option 1 touches the migration flow's auth step end to end (backend command swap + the source-auth screen becomes a password screen, mirroring `PdsAuthScreen`), plus an ADR-0021 amendment noting migration joins the claim flow on the password path — and then a new TestFlight build. Want me to build it now, or is this one you want to take like MM-289?

input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (b), on device: the orchestrator failed at create-destination-account with `SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED` ("Couldn't authorize with the destination PDS").

## Evidence (curl-reproduced against bsky.social)

`getServiceAuth?aud=did:web:ezpds-staging.up.railway.app&lxm=com.atproto.server.createAccount`:

| Credential tier | Result |
|---|---|
| Full session (password createSession) | ✅ mints token |
| Privileged app password | ✅ mints token |
| Plain app password / OAuth `transition:generic` (what the wallet holds) | ❌ `InvalidRequest: insufficient access to request a service auth token for the following method: com.atproto.server.createAccount` |

The reference PDS gates service-token minting for privileged methods at the privileged tier. The orchestrator's design assumption — `transition:generic` suffices for a *self-signed* migration's source calls — holds for repo/blobs/preferences/deactivate but not this mint. MM-289's sibling.

Leg (r) masked it: Custos's `require_rpc` lets `transition:generic` mint any lxm (an MM-292-family laxness — noted there).

## Fix

Switch the outbound-migration **source login** from the OAuth PKCE pair (`prepare_source_auth`/`complete_source_auth`) to the claim flow's password `createSession` machinery (ADR-0021 pattern): full-session Bearer client, HTTPS guard, account-match guard, email-2FA support. One consistent path for bsky and Custos sources (legs b/c/d). MigrationSourceAuthScreen becomes a password form mirroring PdsAuthScreen. Amend ADR-0021: migration source login joins the claim flow on the password path — a full session is required to mint the `createAccount` service token, per reference enforcement.

Rejected alternative: requesting `transition:chat.bsky` to reach the privileged OAuth tier — semantically wrong (DM access to migrate) and fragile.
